title: American soldier accused of spying in U.S. custody after U.K. arrest
summary: Federal Bureau of Investigation director Kash Patel said that the soldier was "a potential threat to national security."
story: A United States Army soldier arrested in the United Kingdom on suspicion that he engaged in espionage linked to Russia has been taken into the custody of the U.S. military, British and American officials said Tuesday.

A U.S. official previously identified the suspect as Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, a senior human resources officer based at Imjin Barracks, home to the headquarters of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. Tyner, 41, joined the Army in 2008 and has been deployed to Afghanistan, Qatar and Iraq.
Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said in a news release that U.S. authorities will continue the investigation. The suspect is expected to be charged soon.

"These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," Taylor said.

The soldier is suspected of violating the U.K.'s National Security Act of 2023 to obtain or disclose protected information and to assist a foreign intelligence service. The London Metropolitan Police said the suspected activity relates to Russia. Federal Bureau of Investigation director Kash Patel said that the soldier was "a potential threat to national security."

He was arrested by the the London Metropolitan Police during a sting operation in Gloucester, about 100 miles west of London, on November 10. The operation involved the Met Police's Counter Terrorism Policing Unit, the U.S. military and the FBI.
"This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement on Tuesday.
Officials have carried out further searches in Gloucestershire, the county where Gloucester is located, related to the investigation, the Metropolitan Police Department said.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters in Moscow last week that Russia had "nothing to do with" the soldier's detention.

U.K. police said the arrest is not related to "any other ongoing Counter Terrorism Policing investigations." The unit is investigating a recent suspected plot at RAF Fairford, a British Royal Air Force base where U.S. troops and aircraft are stationed. The U.S. military removed its bombers from that base after the security incident.

Five British men and one U.K.-Iranian national were arrested in late September. Last week, the U.S. Justice Department announced that three people it accuses of being Iran-backed operatives were charged with plotting a terrorist attack at the site. One suspect is in custody in New York, and the other two are not in custody, two sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

Actor Larry Poindexter died Wednesday awaiting surgery days after being struck by a car in Los Angeles. He was 66.

Poindexter, a character actor known for roles on such television shows as "JAG" and "Days of Our Lives," died suddenly Wednesday morning in a hospital while awaiting surgery to repair broken ribs sustained in the crash, as Deadline first reported. He had been struck by a vehicle Friday while crossing a street in his Studio City neighborhood to pick up food. An official cause of death has not been released.

story: Fresh off winning Entertainer, Album, and Female Vocalist of the Year, the "Choosin’ Texas" hitmaker reflects on her career-defining night backstage at Bridgestone Arena.
The 60th CMA Awards took place Wednesday night at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee, with Lainey Wilson returning as the award show's host for the third year in a row.

Ella Langley capped off a historic night at the CMA Awards by winning entertainer of the year. With wins for entertainer, female vocalist, album ("Dandelion"), single, song, and music video of the year ("Choosin' Texas"), she became the first woman in CMA history, and only the second artist ever, alongside Alan Jackson in 2002, to sweep the ceremony's top five honors in a single night.

title: Ella Langley dominates CMA Awards with major wins as Taylor Swift makes stunning return to stage
summary: Ella Langley dominates the CMAs as she wins big while Taylor Swift makes her return after decade-long absence.
story: Fresh off winning Entertainer, Album, and Female Vocalist of the Year, the "Choosin’ Texas" hitmaker reflects on her career-defining night backstage at Bridgestone Arena.
The 60th annual Country Music Association Awards took place live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday night.
Ella Langley dominated the awards ceremony, as the winner of entertainer of the year, the biggest award of the night.
While accepting the award, she joked that the crowd must be sick of her already, getting a laugh from those in the room.
"This isn't real life," she said while accepting the award. "Thank you, Jesus, I'm at a loss for words," she added, before saying, "This has been the most special night."
Langley won album of the year for her album, "Dandelion." (Michael Buckner/Billboard via Getty Images)
As she swept all the categories she was nominated in, Lainey Wilson brought out a bedazzled broom for her, telling her she knew she had it prepared as she knew Langley was going to sweep the show.

Langley also won music video of the year before the broadcast. "Choosin' Texas" was named as the music video of the year winner during Good Morning America Wednesday morning. The record-breaking hit also won single of the year and song of the year.
WATCH: Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert and the 'Choosin' Texas' team pose with their CMA Awards

Later in the show, Langley got teary-eyed as she accepted the award for album of the year, for her album, "Dandelion," noting it took two years to make. She was speechless while accepting the award and received a standing ovation from the audience.
Langley joked the audience must be sick of her after winning entertainer of the year. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
"I’m at a loss for words. I don’t know what to say," she said in her speech. "I love country music and I love what I do."
Her wins also resulted in two wins for Miranda Lambert, who is credited as a producer on the song.
Langley continued her winning streak later on in the show when she took home the award for female vocalist of the year, beating out Lambert, Musgraves, Moroney and Wilson for the honor.

"I have so much love and respect for every single person and every single woman in this category," she said while accepting the award. "This is what I have lived and breathed not only just the past seven years that I moved to Nashville, but genuinely my whole entire life. I haven’t wanted to do another thing. There wasn’t anything on my heart. I never had a plan B. I was never gonna have a plan b. If I was still playing cover gigs with a tip jar out in front of me for four hours I’d still be doing this."
Langley won female vocalist of the year. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)

Rising star Langley led the pack with 9 nominations, tying Lainey Wilson and Lambert's all-time record for the most nods by a female artist in a single year. Her win for single of the year left Taylor Swift going home empty-handed tonight, which didn't stop Taylor Swift from cheering for her as she went up to accept the award.
Swift made her big return to the CMA Awards – after last attending in 2016. Her single, "I Knew It, I Knew You," is nominated for single of the year.
The singer took the stage to perform at the CMA Awards for the first time in 13 years, starting her performance with her nominated song, before transitioning into one of her classic hits, "Our Song."
Lambert also had a moment on stage with Kacey Musgraves, when the two sang their hit duet, "Horses and Divorces," from Musgraves' latest album, "Middle of Nowhere."
Taylor Swift and Ella Langley both have big nights at the 2026 CMA Awards. (Getty Images)
The song references the rumored feud between the two singers, with them patching things up earlier this year.
Zach Top honored veteran and military families, bringing one on stage and surprising them with the return of their son from service.

In addition to her performance with Musgraves, Lambert took the stage once again with Langley to sing their song, "Snakeskin Boots" for the first time on television. The two matched in their versions of brown dresses with snakeskin print and fringe as they commanded the stage during their performance.
Lambert and Langley sang their song together on stage. (Michael Buckner/Billboard via Getty Images)

Brooks & Dunn won vocal duo of the year for the 17th time in a row at this year’s award show. In addition, the duo also received the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award, which was presented to them by Swift.
Prior to Swift handing them the award, Luke Bryan took to the stage alongside Brothers Osborne, HARDY, Marcus King and Halestorm to pay tribute to the iconic duo.
WATCH: Miranda Lambert poses with her CMA Awards following her wins

Little Big Town announced Chris Stapleton as the winner of male vocalist of the year. The musician took the stage earlier in the evening with both Mumford & Sons to sing "Here" and Stephen Wilson Jr. to sing, "I’m a Song."
Chris Stapleton won male vocalist of the year at the CMA Awards. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
During his speech he encouraged fans to follow their dreams, and dedicated the award to his mother, who died last year around this time.
"She always told me that I could be whatever I wanted to be, and turns out that was true," he said.

Lady A introduced Tim McGraw to the stage to perform, "Don’t Take the Girl" for the first time on the CMA stage, as he is one of the Country Music Hall of Fame inductees this year. It was an intimate performance with the majority of the stage lights turned off save for a few spotlights behind him.
Musgraves and Lambert performed "Horses and Divorces" at the award show. (Frank Micelotta/The Walt Disney Company via Getty Images)
Wilson returned to host the event for the third consecutive time, her second solo. Wilson is also nominated for entertainer of the year, which she won in 2023 and 2025.
She also took to the stage during the show to perform her hit song, "Just A Woman."

Megan Moroney blew fans away while strumming on her pink guitar as she sang "Beautiful Things" into her pink microphone. During her performance, fans surrounding the stage held up pink roses, while everyone in the arena swayed to the beat as with their flashlights lighting up the crowd.
Moroney sang into a pink microphone as she strummed a pink guitar. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)

Tucker Wetmore got the crowd pumped with his performance of "Who Told You That," encouraging the crowd to get up and dance. While singing, he enthusiastically played the piano which was surrounded by a circle of fire on the stage.

The show began with a tribute to Dolly Parton. Parton was one of the most decorated figures in CMA Awards history, earning 45 nominations and winning 10 trophies over her career, including entertainer of the year in 1978, two female vocalist of the year awards, and the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016.
Wilson performing during the show. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
Beyond her wins, she also helped define the telecast itself, famously co-hosting the ceremony in 1988 and returning in 2019 to co-host alongside Carrie Underwood and Reba McEntire.
'GOD HAS BEEN SO GOOD TO ME': ELLA LANGLEY REACTS TO INCREDIBLE NINE CMA AWARDS NOMINATIONS
Parton died on August 25, 2026, at age 80 in Nashville following a brief, private battle with cancer, roughly a year and a half after the passing of her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean.
Dolly Parton was honored at the 2026 CMA Awards on Wednesday night. (Getty Images)

Taylor Swift attends the 60th Annual CMA Awards at Bridgestone Arena on Nov. 18, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. (Billboard via Getty Images)
At the start of the show, Wilson made lighthearted jokes about Swift and Travis Kelce's mega Madison Square Garden wedding.

While Swift, Wilson and Langley have already taken the stage for solo performances,  Luke Combs, Megan Moroney, The Red Clay Strays, Tucker Wetmore, Vince Gill, and Zach Top are still set to perform.
Cody Johnson had to back out of the 2026 CMA Awards at the last minute. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic/Getty Images)

title: Jeff Bezos says he was 'heavily involved' in picking Robert Pattinson as James Bond
summary: Jeff Bezos says Robert Pattinson's fame initially worked against him in the James Bond casting until old-fashioned screen tests made it obvious.
story: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos said the team was ‘slightly biased a little against’ Robert Pattinson because of his fame before screen tests made it ‘so obvious.’
When it came to naming Robert Pattinson the next James Bond, Jeff Bezos says he was "heavily involved" in the selection process.

During an appearance at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference Tuesday, the Amazon founder opened up about the casting process and said the team initially considered choosing a lesser-known actor.

"Yes, I was heavily involved. We ran a really tight process, and we made the final decision on Friday. We down selected. There were a big group initially. We down selected to five finalists," Bezos said, according to The Associated Press.
ROBERT PATTINSON’S JAMES BOND CASTING COULD BRING 'DARKER,' 'MOODIER' TWIST AS FANS CRAVE CLASSIC 007: EXPERT
Jeff Bezos was "heavily involved" in Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond. (Getty Images)

"And then we did real, old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists, and it was — it was really interesting, you know? Full costume, real sets, other actors with them. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists. And then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all those screen tests and reviewing all that."
While Bezos said all the other actors were "extraordinarily talented," there was something about Pattinson.
WATCH: Jeff Bezos was ‘heavily involved’ in casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond
ROBERT PATTINSON IS THE NEW JAMES BOND; CAN HE BECOME THE HERO THE WEST NEEDS?
"By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob and his performances," Bezos said.

"And it was kind of immediately undebated. Denis, the director, we all sort of gravitated. ... By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening test, it was so obvious. He is James Bond."
Robert Pattinson will portray the next James Bond.  (Stephane Cardinale/Corbis)
The news of Pattinson's casting was announced Monday.

I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team."

The first trailer, which debuted Nov. 18, offered fans a glimpse of Powell as Aubrey King, a country music superstar whose career comes crashing down after a public breakup with his pop star girlfriend Missy, played by "Outer Banks" star Madelyn Cline.
King discovers Missy is cheating on him, but she goes on to make a breakup anthem that makes it seem like he was unfaithful.

title: Russell Brand could be banned from contacting wife after 'appalling' prison message
summary: Russell Brand's prison message read by wife Laura Brand is being urgently investigated, and he could face a communication ban under the Prison Rules 1999.
story: Fox News senior foreign affairs correspondent Greg Palkot reports on Russell Brand's 10-year sentencing after his conviction for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. The judge criticized Brand's conduct, while his attorneys are expected to appeal the verdict.
Russell Brand could face serious consequences — including being banned from communicating with his wife, Laura Brand — after releasing an "appalling" message from behind prison bars.

According to the regulations governing prisons in England and Wales, authorities can restrict a prisoner's contact with the outside world.  Brand — who was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault — could face such restrictions if found to have violated rules governing outside communications.
On Sunday, Brand claimed he is "not guilty" in a message read by Laura during an episode of the couple's weekly Sunday Service YouTube vlog.
RUSSELL BRAND’S WIFE DEFENDS ACTOR AT RAPE TRIAL WHILE ADMITTING HIS PAST MONOGAMY STRUGGLES
Russell Brand was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison last week after being convicted of rape. (James Manning)

Shortly after the message was shared publicly, a spokesperson for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a statement to Deadline: "This is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he’s found to have broken the rules."

"Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances. Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."
BEAR GRYLLS ADDRESSES RUSSELL BRAND'S BAPTISM, CALLS VICTIMS 'HEROES OF THE DAY' AFTER VERDICT

On Monday, Lord Chancellor and Secretary of State Alex Norris wrote on X: "The broadcast of a statement from Russell Brand is completely unacceptable. Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims."
"This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules."
RUSSELL BRAND SPARKS PRISON INVESTIGATION AFTER WIFE READS DEFIANT MESSAGE FOLLOWING RAPE CONVICTION

Trial attorney and former prosecutor Imran Ansari questioned the backlash to Brand’s message during an appearance on the "Crime & Justice with Donna Rotunno" podcast, arguing that the statement asserted innocence without targeting his accusers.
WATCH LATEST EPISODE OF ‘CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO’
"They’re declaring that innocence without necessarily attacking anyone. They don’t bring up a woman at all," Ansari said.

Asked about the potential consequences, Ansari suggested Brand could face restrictions on communications with reporters or other media figures, but acknowledged he did not know what action, if any, prison officials would take.
"It’s typical that a prisoner who maintains their innocence will release statements," he said. "I don’t know what Russell Brand now will face because of this."
Russell Brand's wife, Laura Brand, took the stand in the actor's rape and sexual assault trial. (Getty Images)
RUSSELL BRAND’S WIFE OPENS UP AFTER COMEDIAN’S RAPE CONVICTION, SHARES MESSAGE FROM IMPRISONED HUSBAND
In the message, Brand claimed his innocence while confirming he is currently being jailed at HMP Littlehey, a prison for individuals who have been convicted of sexual offenses.

"Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening," Laura read from a notebook.
Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court in London on Oct. 29, 2026, ahead of his trial on rape and sexual assault charges. He has denied all charges. (Getty Images)

"The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do. I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey. Little as in small, and hey as in, ‘Hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe. The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated," she continued. "And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone."

"I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me. Let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us."

"Please support my treasured wife and family. I feel your prayers, your brother in Christ. Russell," she concluded the note.
Brand was sentenced on Nov. 9.
RUSSELL BRAND FOUND GUILTY OF ONE COUNT OF RAPE AND THREE COUNTS OF SEXUAL ASSAULT
Brand has maintained his innocence.  (Mike Marsland/WireImage)

title: John Madden role pushes Nicolas Cage to dramatic physical transformation with ‘brutal’ diet, prosthetics
summary: Nicolas Cage gained over 25 pounds on pasta and bread, then added 30 more with prosthetics to physically transform into John Madden for the biopic.
story: Nicolas Cage discussed which one of his former roles was his favorite to play, listing Castor Troy in "Face/Off" as one of the top ones.
Nicolas Cage's radical transformation to portray John Madden in the upcoming biopic about the NFL legend included packing on the pounds and the prosthetics.
In addition to a number of prosthetics, Cage, 62, admitted he gained more than 25 pounds to physically embody his character for Prime Video's "Madden."
"I just enjoyed my pasta and my sourdough bread, which I don’t normally do," Cage told People magazine.
THE CAST OF 'MADDEN' HITS THE RED CARPET TO TALK ABOUT WHETHER THEY'VE CHOWED DOWN ON TURDUCKEN
Nicolas Cage gained weight and wore a slew of prosthetics to portray NFL legend John Madden. (Chuck Zlotnick/Prime © Amazon Content Services LLC)
"I mean, it’s pretty brutal. Two premier protein shakes and one meal a day. It’s usually a Caesar salad."
He added, "But with that, I got to enjoy the pasta and then I added — look, I’m 62, so I’m not going to gain 60 pounds. That’s dangerous. But I added the other 30 with [prosthetics]."
NICOLAS CAGE TURNED DOWN PARTS IN TWO BIG FRANCHISE MOVIES FOR ROLES HE THOUGHT WERE BETTER
Cage admitted that while he enjoyed packing on the pounds, returning to his pre-Madden size was slightly more challenging.
"Not really," Cage said, when asked if the weight came off easily. "A lot of days in the gym on the elliptical. I still do it. I’m always on the elliptical for a couple of hours a day."
Nicolas Cage portrays John Madden while Christian Bale got into character as his best friend, Raiders icon Al Davis. (2026 Amazon Content Services LLC)

Directed by David O. Russell, the film follows Madden from Super Bowl-winning coach of the Oakland Raiders to his role in creating arguably one of the most influential video game franchises – Madden NFL ​with Electronic Arts.

Kathryn Hahn said Cage's transformation didn't stop once the prosthetics were on. (Chuck Zlotnick/Prime)

Cage revealed that his own father worked in education as a professor of comparative literature, and he "grew to love" Madden even more after realizing that John was "a teacher first."

Nicolas Cage stars alongside Christian Bale in Prime Video's "Madden." (Prime Video)

title: 'The Vow' host Chris Harrison says young people are ditching dating apps, turning to church
summary: Chris Harrison says young people are rejecting dating apps and turning to faith, inspiring his new Fox Nation series "Chris Harrison's The Vow."
story: The host of "Chris Harrison's The Vow" told Fox News Digital why he believes younger generations are turning toward faith and seeking deeper connections as his new dating series premieres on Fox Nation.
Chris Harrison believes young people are turning away from dating apps and looking toward faith as they search for meaningful relationships.

The television host, who returned to reality dating television with the premiere of "Chris Harrison's The Vow" on Fox Nation, told Fox News Digital that he and the show's producers have noticed what he describes as a growing movement among younger generations seeking something deeper than modern dating culture offers.
"Young people searching for something, going to church more than their parents are," Harrison said.
'CHRIS HARRISON’S THE VOW’ SPARKS ‘TRAD WIFE’ DEBATE AMONG CONTESTANTS AS EMOTIONS RUN HIGH
Chris Harrison returned to reality television as the host of Fox Nation's "The Vow," which takes a different approach to modern dating. (Getty Images)

"Attending youth nights in incredible numbers at churches and temples and all these organizations getting together around faith. So clearly they're searching for something, looking for something, and at the same time, dating apps are being rejected."
Harrison suggested that technology, while making it easier to meet people, may also be contributing to less meaningful relationships.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"So, you know, maybe this world, technologically speaking, that's moving so fast and trying to make our lives easier, and maybe trying to make connections easier, but are also less meaningful," he said.
"And so I think 'The Vow' is maybe slowing things down a little bit, saying, 'Hey, let's see if we really can find love in this modern world.'"
WATCH: CHRIS HARRISON SAYS YOUNG PEOPLE ARE REJECTING DATING APPS IN SEARCH OF SOMETHING 'MORE MEANINGFUL'

The new series follows Jace Cates, a 30-year-old mortgage loan officer from Oregon, as he meets 10 women hoping to find a husband. Set in the Texas Hill Country, the show focuses on faith, family values and the possibility of building a lasting marriage.
The first two episodes premiered Nov. 11, with new episodes scheduled to debut every Wednesday.
For Harrison, returning to television with a project centered on relationships has been a rewarding experience.
"If I'm being honest, it has felt very, very good to step back into the world of not just reality TV, but dating and love and helping people find love," he told Fox News Digital.
"I just feel more than ever, we need love."
Harrison said the early response to the series has been encouraging.
WATCH: FOX NATION'S ‘THE VOW’ LEADING MAN JACE CATES PREVIEWS NEW FAITH-BASED DATING SHOW
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"But with the early returns that we have seen, the response from fans, people are loving it, and they seem to be enjoying the fact that I'm back on their TVs, which feels really good. It's kind of cathartic."
The television personality explained that he wanted to create a dating experience that reflected the changing priorities he believes younger generations are embracing.

"I think seeing the need for a show that is truly about love and romance, and seeing again this societal movement by the young people in this generation kind of asking for something deeper, more meaningful," he said.
Harrison said he and the producers wanted to create an environment where participants could have serious conversations about their futures.
"And so we've tried to make the most authentic, intentional environment so these people can really find love."
Jace Cates, 30, is searching for his future wife among 10 women on Fox Nation's faith-focused dating series "Chris Harrison's The Vow." (Fox Nation)
The series has already sparked conversations about traditional marriage, with several women expressing interest in becoming stay-at-home mothers while others hope to continue pursuing their careers.
Harrison said he welcomed the different perspectives, particularly because the contestants felt comfortable discussing their faith and expectations for marriage.
"I'm really glad the ladies and Jace felt really comfortable speaking of their faith and speaking of what they want and hope in a marriage, in a family," he said.
"They're asking those questions that you should be."
He explained that the women represent a wide range of expectations for their future relationships.
"There are some women that want to be stay-at-home moms. They want to just be a supportive wife. Then there are some that want to be CEOs and run the world."
WATCH: CHRIS HARRISON WEIGHS IN ON CONTROVERSY SURROUNDING TRADITIONAL MARRIAGE: 'IT'S GOING TO BE DIFFERENT FOR EVERYBODY'
Harrison praised Jace for approaching the subject with an open mind.
"And what I love about Jace is, when he was talking about what he thought about traditional marriage, it was all of that," he said.
CHRIS HARRISON RETURNS TO REALITY TV WITH 'THE VOW,' FOX NATION'S FIRST-EVER DATING SHOW
"It was just being a champion for my partner, just being there for my wife, whatever that looks like."
The host acknowledged that the phrase "traditional marriage" can carry different meanings depending on the person.
"Well, I think, you know, many things in this day and age become fragmented and political," he said.
"And in this context, and I hope you'll watch 'The Vow,' because in this context, it really is more about faith and about their values and morals."
Harrison said the show isn't meant to tell viewers what a marriage should look like, but rather to encourage conversations about what works for different couples.
"I like leaning into the debate. I like leading into the conversation and maybe leaning into the uncomfortable a little bit, pushing ourselves."
Faith also plays a central role in the series, with contestants openly discussing prayer, abstinence and their religious beliefs.
Harrison said the decision to cast people of faith was intentional, but emphasized that the women have different perspectives when it comes to intimacy and relationships.
"Some are kind of born again, celibate. Some are, you know, saving themselves," he said.
He added that the variety of experiences allows viewers to connect with different contestants.
"It's not just one size fits all. That's not the real world."
Harrison also reflected on his own marriage to Lauren Zima, explaining that finding love when he least expected it reinforced his belief that people shouldn't give up on relationships.
The couple recently celebrated their third wedding anniversary after exchanging vows in Napa Valley and later hosting a larger celebration in Austin, Texas.
Chris Harrison and wife Lauren Zima recently celebrated three years of marriage. The couple worked together as executive producers on Fox Nation's "The Vow." (Getty Images)
"Maybe that's the lesson, is never give up. When you least expect it, maybe expect it the most, but have faith," he said.
"And I hope that's what 'The Vow' will do, is give people faith that love still exists."
Harrison, who serves as an executive producer of the series alongside his wife, said working together has made the project especially meaningful.
"You know, I think doing the show with the love of your life, first of all, it's an honor and a privilege to get to do that," he said.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
"We're bringing our love and we're bringing our faith. But we're not imposing it on anybody."
Ultimately, Harrison hopes the series encourages viewers to reconsider what they want from modern relationships.
"What we're hearing from young people is that the bar is on the floor," he said.
He explained that the goal was to raise expectations by focusing on genuine commitment rather than casual dating.
"And the reaction so far has been, 'Thank you. Thank you for providing this environment. Thank you for doing a show like this.'"

On Sunday, Brand — who was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault — claimed he is "not guilty" in a message read by his wife, Laura Brand, during an episode of the couple's weekly Sunday Service YouTube vlog.

"Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening," Laura read from a notebook.

summary: Phil Collins says a full-time nurse helps manage his medication as he adjusts to life off the road, with physio three times a week keeping him moving.
story: Speaking at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, the music icon opens up about living on his own, spending "a lot of time in hospital," and working three times a week to stay mobile.
English singer and drummer Phil Collins relies on a full-time nurse during his "enforced" time off from touring.
During an interview with Fox News Digital at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction ceremony, Collins said that adjusting to not performing has been easy.

"Adjusting is easy. I spent a lot of time in hospital with various things, so that was enforced, you know, time off. But I just sit at home, I live on my own, I got a nurse there all the time to make sure I take medication on time, and I've got my assistant who is always there," Collins began.

"I got a nurse there all the time to make sure I take medication on time, and I've got my assistant who is always there."

title: Robert Pattinson’s James Bond casting could bring 'darker,' 'moodier' twist as fans crave classic 007: expert
summary: Robert Pattinson calls his James Bond casting "the honor of a lifetime," but critics say his brooding Batman past makes him a risky pick for 007.
story: Former Bond girl Alison Papworth shares why she wants the next 007 to stay true to the books as speculation swirls over the role.
James Bond may never miss, but Robert Pattinson's casting as the next iconic British secret agent was positively shocking to fans across the world.

Pattinson, 40, called the role "the honor of a lifetime," in a statement released Monday where "Dune" director Denis Villeneuve was also tapped to bring Bond back to the big screen following Daniel Craig's 15-year reign as 007.
Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo admitted he was "shaken, not stirred" by the casting choice.
ROBERT PATTINSON NAMED NEXT JAMES BOND
Actor Robert Pattinson at the screening of the film "Primetime" at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival in Italy, on Sept. 5. (Laurent KOFFEL/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images)

"As a huge fan of the Ian Fleming novels, Pattinson isn’t quite what I envisioned or what I think fans were hoping for," Arroyo told Fox News Digital. "After five Bond films with Daniel Craig in the lead, it was probably time to bring back some of the fun and charm that Pierce Brosnan and Roger Moore brought to the franchise."
He noted how Pattinson was known for his "brooding and dark qualities," a contrast to the more masculine qualities a Bond character usually brings to the screen.
FORMER BOND GIRL SAYS NEXT 007 SHOULD BE 'ANOTHER GORGEOUS MAN' AS JAMES BOND DECISION
"As a huge fan of the Ian Fleming novels, Pattinson isn’t quite what I envisioned or what I think fans were hoping for."

"Fun and a light touch is not the first thing that comes to mind when you think of his filmography," Arroyo said. "His Batman was a pretty dreary affair, the sequel of which I could care less about seeing. Bond also requires a certain physicality and strength – he is an assassin after all."
Arroyo believed Henry Cavill "would have been a much better choice all round."
Sean Connery starred as James Bond 007 in the '64 film "Goldfinger." (Screen Archives/Getty Images)

"But it sounds like MGM/Amazon wants to give audiences a darker, moodier Bond – just when the public is craving a good, old-fashioned escape. We’ll see if audiences wish this new Bond to ‘Live or Let Die.’"
Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson’s casting on social media with a brief snippet of the actor emerging from the shadows with a gun.
PIERCE BROSNAN BACKS 'FANTASTIC BEASTS' STAR FOR NEXT JAMES BOND, PREDICTS FANS WILL BE 'BLOWN AWAY'

"Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007," Villeneuve said in a statement.
"I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin."
Daniel Craig starred as the British secret agent from 2006–21. (Greg Williams/Eon Productions via Getty Images)
Adrienne Uthe, founder of Kronus Communications, exclusively told Fox News Digital that Pattinson was a "risk" to the franchise.

"He's going in as the underdog, period," Uthe said. "To win over the Connery people, the Brosnan people, the Craig people, he can’t just be good — he has to do it better than what’s been done before. That’s the bar when you take a role this iconic, you have to prove you’re actually worth it."
Pattinson found global fame years ago as telepathic vampire Edward Cullen in the "Twilight" series, which collectively grossed more than $3.3 billion worldwide.

"He can’t just be good – He has to do it better than what’s been done before. That’s the bar when you take a role this iconic, you have to prove you’re actually worth it."
Uthe noted that while a younger audience already knows his face and therein may show up to watch him as Bond, there's still a risk of "watering down the brand."
Pierce Brosnan stars as 007 opposite Denise Richards as Dr. Christmas Jones in the '99 James Bond film "The World Is Not Enough." (Keith Hamshere/Getty Images)
"Bond is established, seasoned, it’s got pedigree — so he has to bring pedigree to it too," Uthe said. "He has to prove he can be taken seriously in a role like Bond."

She added, "Now, underdogs can win. People forget Daniel Craig got torn apart when he was cast — too blonde, too rough, wrong guy — and then 'Casino Royale' came out and that was the end of that conversation. So it’s doable. But he has to earn it on screen, nobody’s handing it to him."

Seven actors have starred as the legendary British spy over the years, a role which first originated on television with Barry Nelson before Sean Connery was tapped to play the secret service agent in the '62 film "Dr. No."

Brand expert Eric Schiffer explained that the franchise may face a fan exodus with a "painfully boring" 007, a contrast to the previous Bonds played by David Niven, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan.
English actor Roger Moore poses for a portrait in London, England, on July 20, 1979. Moore portrayed James Bond in the Bond series. (Getty Images)
"Pattinson as Bond is a slap in the face to James, to 007's character, and largely because of his prior history and the Bond character himself," Schiffer told Fox News Digital.
"He failed as Batman. It was a horror show, and prior to that he was the 'Twilight' guy with too much makeup. We're now James Bond? Well, what happened?"

title: Prince William draws hard line on Harry, Meghan’s royal future as King Charles leaves door open: experts
summary: King Charles may keep a personal bond with Prince Harry, but Prince William reportedly sees no path to a working royal return for the Sussexes.
story: Royal commentator Kinsey Schofield explains why Prince William is reportedly not prioritizing reconciliation with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle amid lingering trust issues.
King Charles may leave the door open to Prince Harry personally while ruling out a royal return.
The monarch and his heir, Prince William, are reportedly drawing a firm line on Harry and Meghan Markle returning to royal duties, despite hopes among royal watchers for a family reconciliation.
"There is no half in, half out concession," Kinsey Schofield, host of the YouTube show "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.
PRINCE WILLIAM HAS 'LEARNED' TO LIVE WITHOUT PRINCE HARRY AS ROYAL FEUD REACHES BREAKING POINT: EXPERT
King Charles III and Prince William are reportedly in agreement that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle should not be working royals again. (Getty Images)

"The Sussexes moving back to Britain does not turn the clock back to January 2020 or reopen negotiations. King Charles may want a personal relationship with his son and grandchildren. William recognizes that his father is entitled to make that decision, but William is entitled to make his own."

"William's responsibilities today extend beyond this family feud," Schofield said. "He's preparing for the future. He's focused on the future. He's raising three children and supporting not only his wife, but his father. So maybe the question isn't when will William reconcile with Harry. Maybe it's whether William believes reconciliation would bring peace and stability into his life. And right now ... Prince William is not convinced that Harry is a peaceful presence."
Prince William, Prince of Wales, departs the Amos Bursary in Hoxton, London, on Oct. 14, 2026, after meeting scholars and alumni. (SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
Schofield's comments came after royal author Russell Myers told People magazine that Charles and William are united in their opposition to the Sussexes representing the royal family.
WATCH: PRINCE WILLIAM SEES NO PATH TO PRINCE HARRY REUNION, EXPERT SAYS
"The king and William are completely united on the Sussexes not representing the royal family," Myers told People. "It's without a doubt how in sync they are on this matter."

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex returned to Britain on Aug. 26, about a week after reports emerged that they planned to relocate to the U.K. for an extended stay with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. Harry has expressed a desire for his children to learn more about their British heritage.

Prince William, Prince of Wales, left, and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, join the Procession following the State Hearse carrying the coffin of Queen Elizabeth II towards St George's Chapel on Sept. 19, 2022, in Windsor, England. A source recently told People magazine that Harry wants to heal his rift with William. (Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

On Sept. 7, Buckingham Palace released a letter sent on behalf of the king confirming that Harry and Meghan remain nonworking royals. The guidance reaffirmed the terms of the couple's 2020 departure from official royal duties. The letter also clarified that the Sussexes' charitable activities remain private and that their royal highness styles are not used.

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, arrive at The Community Recording Studio, a youth and community charity, during their visit to Nottingham on Oct. 15, 2026, in Nottingham, England. (Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace and Kensington Palace for comment.
Schofield said her sources indicated that while the king is open to mending his relationship with Harry, William is more focused on protecting the monarchy and avoiding further family conflict.
Prince William, Prince of Wales, attends Earthshot's "Cricket On The Mall" on Oct. 13, 2026, in London. (Getty Images)
"My sources tell me that reconciliation with Harry and Meghan is simply not a priority for the Prince of Wales," Schofield said.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Prince William, Prince of Wales, attends the 2026 Tusk Conservation Awards at Raffles London at The OWO on Nov. 11, 2026, in London, England. As Royal Patron of Tusk, Prince William helped launch the awards in 2013 to recognize dedicated, forward-thinking individuals who are conservation leaders and wildlife rangers across Africa. (Getty Images)

"That doesn't mean William spends his days angry with Harry. Quite the opposite. William has a packed agenda. He has his family, his responsibilities as the Prince of Wales and an increasingly significant role supporting the king. And when Harry and Meghan walked away from royal life, other members of the family had to absorb some of the responsibility they'd left behind."

"William also has personally been through an incredibly difficult six years," Schofield said. "He lost Prince Philip. He lost Queen Elizabeth. His father was diagnosed with cancer. His wife Catherine was diagnosed with cancer. Meanwhile, Harry was absent and publicly hurling accusations at the royal family. Trust was damaged and trust isn't magically restored because Harry and Meghan have moved back to Britain."

Britain's Prince William, Prince of Wales, reacts as he meets with scholars and alumni of The Amos Bursary in London on Oct. 14, 2026. Founded by Baroness Valerie Amos and Colleen Amos in 2009, The Amos Bursary is a charity that supports high-achieving young people of African and Caribbean heritage. (POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
"If Prince William can't trust Harry as a brother, he certainly can't trust him as a representative of the monarchy he will one day inherit," Schofield added.

Prince Harry attends the opening of the Lost Screen Memorial exhibition at the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, on Nov. 10, 2026. The exhibition honors children who lost their lives due to online harms and aims to amplify the voices of bereaved families. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

Harry has had a strained relationship with members of the royal family since he and Meghan stepped back as senior working royals in 2020 and moved to California. While he has been in contact with his father and privately met with the king and Queen Camilla at Highgrove in July, his relationship with William remains strained, People reported. According to the outlet, the brothers have not been in contact.
People reported that the king and his younger son have spoken "at least once" since Harry's return to Britain.

King Charles III makes his way through gathered crowds during a visit to Surrey Street Market in Croydon, England, on Nov. 13, 2026. The visit marks both His Majesty's 78th birthday and the market's 750th anniversary. (Getty Images)

"William's view is clear — any relationship his father has with Harry or the Sussexes as a family is entirely up to him," Myers said. "But looking toward the future, he will have no relationship with them, in a working or private capacity whatsoever."

Prince Charles, Prince of Wales, Prince William, Duke of Cambridge, and Prince Harry attend commemorations for the 100th anniversary of the Battle of Vimy Ridge on April 9, 2017, in Lille, France. (WireImage)

British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that she isn't surprised Charles and William agree on the Sussexes' royal status, even as they reportedly take different approaches to a possible family reconciliation.
The Prince and Princess of Wales have been supporting the monarch. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"Prince William has publicly pledged his loyalty and allegiance to King Charles," Chard said. "Obviously, King Charles has loyalty to his son, Prince William, heir to the throne. He realizes that William is concentrating on his future kingship."
"Prince William has strict personal and institutional boundaries in place," Chard noted.
Prince William, Prince of Wales, looks on following a visit to Aberfan Memorial Garden to mark the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan disaster on Oct. 21, 2026, in Merthyr Tydfil, Wales. (Getty Images)
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital that his sources said William has made his feelings about Harry and Meghan's potential return to royal duties clear in private.

"Prince William is very much opposed to Harry and Meghan coming back into the royal fold and has made his private feelings abundantly clear on the subject," Turner said. "But I feel Charles will no doubt create ways which will benefit Harry and Meghan."

"In many ways, Harry wants to see the issues with his brother resolved," Turner said. "But my understanding is when William becomes king, the royal family will be a very tight circle. William takes the monarchy to heart."

Prince William, Prince of Wales, and Catherine, Princess of Wales, visit The Commons, a project transforming a church into a self-sustaining community centre, during their visit to Northern Ireland on Oct. 9, 2026, in Belfast, Northern Ireland. (WireImage)
Royal author Simon Vigar told People that William and his wife, Kate Middleton, are taking a "keep calm and carry on" approach to headlines surrounding the Sussexes' return to the U.K.
"They see it as a sideshow and ancient history," Vigar told People.
British royals expert Hilary Fordwich previously told Fox News Digital there's no feud between Prince William and his father, King Charles III. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"They are shining a light on things that are important to them," Ailsa Anderson, a former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II, told People. "What they don't want is all this other noise becoming a distraction."

Britain's Prince William, Prince of Wales and Britain's Catherine, Princess of Wales arrive for a state banquet at Windsor Castle, Windsor, on Oct. 20, 2026, the first day of a three-day State Visit to the United Kingdom by the sultan of Oman. (Aaron Chown/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
Vigar also wondered whether next year's 30th anniversary of Princess Diana's death could offer the brothers an opportunity to reconcile.
"Diana would have hated all this and would have banged their heads together and wouldn't have allowed [the rift] to happen," Vigar said.
Diana, Princess of Wales pictured on Dec. 3, 1993. (Getty Images)
Schofield, however, disagreed with the suggestion that Diana would have pushed her sons to reconcile.

Princess Diana at a state reception in Melbourne in October 1988. (Getty Images)

"I'm always slightly uncomfortable when people invoke Princess Diana and say Diana would want the boys to reconcile," Schofield said. "None of us know what Diana would think about everything that's happened since her death. But we do know from Diana's own pattern of behavior when she believed someone had violated her trust, she was perfectly capable of cutting that person out of her life."
Still, some royal commentators hold out hope that William may eventually follow his father's lead and consider reconciling with Harry.
Prince William and Prince Harry are seen together in 2021. (Getty Images)

"It's clearly incredibly difficult. The trust has broken down," Anderson told People. "Let's hope it's not broken completely, and there's a chink in the armor on both sides, and there could be some sort of reconciliation. But that's not happening anytime soon."

title: Popular alcoholic drinks linked to sudden kidney damage in 14-year study
summary: Beer and hard liquor drinkers face a sharply higher risk of acute kidney injury, a UK Biobank study finds, while red and white wine showed no such link.
story: Josh Gowin explains how research has shifted the understanding of alcohol's health risks, including its association with reduced brain volume, as drinking habits and social norms continue to change.

People who regularly drink beer or hard liquor face a significantly higher risk of sudden kidney damage than light drinkers, while wine drinkers do not show the same increased risk, according to a large British study.
Researchers at Anglia Ruskin University analyzed health and lifestyle data from 250,791 adult drinkers in the UK Biobank database, tracking them for an average of 14 years.
Over that time, 10,335 participants developed acute kidney injury, a serious condition in which the kidneys suddenly stop filtering waste from the blood properly.
IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE
The study, published in the journal Scientific Reports, challenges a longstanding medical assumption that alcohol harms the kidneys mainly as a secondary consequence of liver disease.
The elevated risk among beer and liquor drinkers continued even after researchers considered liver disease and a wide range of other health and lifestyle factors.

The elevated risk for beer and liquor drinkers persisted even after accounting for liver disease, suggesting alcohol may damage the kidneys directly through inflammation rather than solely as a secondary effect of liver harm. (iStock)

"Acute kidney injury is a serious condition that can lead to chronic kidney disease, kidney failure and an increased risk of dying early," lead author Rudolph Schutte, an associate professor of cardiovascular epidemiology at Anglia Ruskin University, said in a university news release.

"While alcohol has traditionally been linked with kidney injury through its impact on the liver, our research suggests that spirits and beer may contribute directly to kidney damage through inflammatory pathways."
HEAVY DRINKING SURGES AMONG AMERICANS IN ONE AGE GROUP AS OTHER GENERATIONS CUT BACK
To compare drinking habits, the researchers divided participants into three groups based on their average weekly consumption of each type of alcohol.
In the U.K., one unit of alcohol equals 8 grams of pure alcohol — a little more than half of a standard U.S. shot of liquor or about half a pint of lower-strength beer.
"Acute kidney injury is a serious condition that can lead to chronic kidney disease, kidney failure and an increased risk of dying early."

Among liquor drinkers, those in the lowest consumption group drank an average of 1.22 units per week. Compared with that group, people who averaged 2.69 units per week were 8.1% more likely to develop acute kidney injury.
Those in the highest tier, averaging 8.73 units per week, had a 25.5% higher risk.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Beer drinkers showed a similar, though smaller, pattern. Compared with light beer drinkers averaging 2.67 units per week, people who drank an average of 6.81 units had a 5.7% higher risk of acute kidney injury.
Those in the highest group, averaging 23.6 units per week, faced a 14.8% higher risk
Regular consumption of beer or hard liquor is linked to a significantly higher risk of sudden kidney damage, whereas wine shows no significant overall association. (iStock)
Researchers found no significant link between red or white wine consumption and a higher risk of acute kidney injury overall.
The authors noted that higher levels of internal inflammation appeared to drive the increased risk seen with other drinks.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"The results provide important population-level evidence supporting laboratory research that has suggested alcohol can directly affect the kidneys," Schutte said.
Beer drinkers saw a smaller increase in risk, rising by 5.7% at an average of 6.81 units per week and 14.8% at 23.6 units per week compared to light beer drinkers. (iStock)
Because the study is observational, it can only identify links between drinking habits and kidney injury, and cannot prove that beer or liquor directly caused the damage.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The authors also warned that the findings do not prove wine protects the kidneys, noting that drinking above 14 units per week, the U.K.’s recommended limit, was tied to higher risk across all drink types, including wine.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Additionally, participants relied on memory to report their average weekly alcohol intake, which can lead to inaccurate estimates or underreporting.
The study also only included adults ages 40 to 69, meaning the results may not apply to younger or older people.

title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' mania comes with serious health risks, doctors warn
summary: Experts warn Grand Theft Auto VI marathon sessions can trigger eye strain, sleep deprivation and problematic gaming amid the PlayStation 5 launch.
story: Psychotherapist Jonathan Alpert addresses concerns surrounding major video game releases, noting that while violent games do not cause real-world crime, excessive screen time can strain health and relationships.

As millions of players prepare for the long-awaited release of "Grand Theft Auto VI," mental health and medical experts are warning that marathon gaming sessions, skipped sleep and obsessive playing habits could have physical and psychological effects.
The latest installment in the blockbuster franchise launches Thursday, Nov. 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, according to New York-based maker Rockstar Games.
"Grand Theft Auto VI" is an action-adventure game set in the fictional state of Leonida, which includes Vice City. Players follow a story while exploring the game’s world and taking on missions.
SKIPPING SLEEP MAY PACK ON POUNDS FASTER THAN YOU THINK, NEW STUDY FINDS
The release is prompting questions about how much time players may devote to the game — including during the workweek.
According to a survey of 1,000 full-time employed U.S. gamers conducted by gaming and esports media company GameSquare, 10% plan to skip work for the game’s launch.
The latest installment in "Grand Theft Auto" launches Thursday, Nov. 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, according to New York-based maker Rockstar Games. (AP Photo/Jeff Chiu)

Another 30% are considering taking time off, and 36% said they would call in sick rather than use planned vacation days. Meanwhile, 42% expect to be less productive at work because of the release, according to the survey.
TOO MUCH SCREEN TIME MAY TRIGGER LASTING BRAIN DELAYS, TOP HEALTH OFFICIAL WARNS

Jonathan Alpert, a psychotherapist based in New York and Washington, D.C., compared the excitement around major game releases to overnight lines for new smartphones, saying fans want to be part of the moment.
DOCTOR REVEALS 4 HIDDEN HEALTH RISKS OF SPENDING TOO MUCH TIME INDOORS

"Video games and social media can be a great distraction from the stress of real life and relationships, but it shouldn't become real life," Alpert, author of "Therapy Nation," told Fox News Digital. "In other words, it shouldn't dominate. It should just be an escape."
Health risks of extended play

"Grand Theft Auto" is an open-world game, meaning players can freely explore a large virtual environment rather than follow a set path from one level to the next. Cleveland Clinic says that freedom, along with the game’s fast-paced action and rewards, can make it hard to stop playing.
"It shouldn't dominate. It should just be an escape."
That constant stream of stimulation can raise a player’s threshold for excitement, making ordinary offline interactions feel flat by comparison, according to Alpert.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Pulling an all-nighter to explore Vice City can also take a toll on the brain. According to the National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute, sleep deficiency impairs concentration, slows reaction times and makes it harder to regulate emotions.

While a single late night is unlikely to cause lasting harm, Alpert said, repeated sleep loss can leave players more vulnerable to anxiety, irritability and difficulty completing basic tasks at school or work.
Sitting at a screen for eight or more hours can trigger neck and back pain, as well as digital eye strain, experts warn. (iStock)

Extended gaming sessions can take a physical toll. Sitting at a screen for eight or more hours can contribute to neck and back pain, repetitive-motion injuries and eyestrain, according to Mayo Clinic.
Research cited by the clinic found that eyestrain affects up to 56% of competitive gamers. Symptoms can include headaches and blurred vision.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Prolonged, uninterrupted sitting can reduce blood flow to the brain and legs, while also affecting blood-vessel function.
"People can get sick if they are sitting at a computer for eight or more hours a day playing games," Alpert cautioned.
Signs of problematic play

The American Psychiatric Association lists nine proposed symptoms of internet gaming disorder, a condition included in the DSM-5-TR for further study. A proposed diagnosis requires five or more of the following symptoms within a year.

Becoming preoccupied with gamingFeeling irritable, anxious or sad when unable to playNeeding to spend more time gaming to feel satisfiedMaking repeated unsuccessful attempts to cut backLosing interest in other activitiesContinuing to play despite problemsLying to family members or others about time spent gamingUsing games to escape or relieve a negative moodJeopardizing or losing a significant relationship, job or educational opportunity because of gaming

"When I look at addictions or people spending too much time online, I look at how [it] has impacted relationships, their work, school, family relations, their health and their finances," Alpert said. "So, when we start to see those suffering, there's a problem."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Adolescents and young adults may be more vulnerable to problematic gaming, while anxiety and depression can co-occur with it, according to Cleveland Clinic.
Ensuring safe play
To participate in launch week in a healthy way, experts recommend setting the following boundaries.

Take regular movement breaks: Stand, walk or stretch for at least five minutes every hour to restore circulation and ease muscle tension, Alpert suggests.Set firm time limits: Alpert advises parents to keep consoles out of teenagers’ bedrooms and limit play to an hour or two after homework is finished. For adults, he recommends prioritizing work and relationships over late-night sessions.Create a mental buffer: After logging off, take a brief breather before jumping back into daily responsibilities.
Take regular movement breaks: Stand, walk or stretch for at least five minutes every hour to restore circulation and ease muscle tension, Alpert suggests.

Set firm time limits: Alpert advises parents to keep consoles out of teenagers’ bedrooms and limit play to an hour or two after homework is finished. For adults, he recommends prioritizing work and relationships over late-night sessions.
Create a mental buffer: After logging off, take a brief breather before jumping back into daily responsibilities.
"You almost have to do a gut check and a reset and remind yourself that what you just saw is fantasy and what you're experiencing now is reality," Alpert added.
Sitting at a screen for eight or more hours can contribute to neck and back pain, repetitive-motion injuries and eyestrain, according to Mayo Clinic. (iStock)
The psychotherapist added that concerns about gaming’s physical effects should be separated from claims that violent games lead to real-world violence.

"Millions of people play violent video games, and they don’t go out there and commit crimes," he said, adding that there is no evidence linking gameplay to real-life violence.

title: Flu activity rises across US as 6 states reach high levels, CDC data shows
summary: Cases of the flu are spiking early nationwide, with the CDC reporting Louisiana at very high activity and influenza A (H1N1) the top virus this season.
story: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel discusses rising flu activity across the U.S. and advances in fertility treatment after actress Hilary Swank reportedly announced her third pregnancy at 52.
Cases of the flu are already cropping up across the country in an early spike.
In its weekly influenza update, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has alerted that seasonal flu activity is "higher than typically observed at this time of year."

About 11% of specimens tested for flu at clinical labs were positive in the week ending Nov. 7, with that percentage rising. The CDC also reported more than 3% of doctors’ office visits were due to flu-like symptoms.
WANT TO DODGE THE FLU THIS YEAR? EAT THESE SECRET-WEAPON IMMUNITY-BOOSTING FOODS
New York, Massachusetts and Hawaii were in the CDC map’s moderate category for influenza-like illness in the week ending Nov. 7 (week 44).

The CDC’s Outpatient Respiratory Illness Activity Map uses reports from ILINet, the agency’s national network of outpatient health care providers, to show how often patients are visiting doctors for respiratory illness symptoms. (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)

California, Tennessee and Oregon were in the high category for influenza-like illness, along with South Carolina and Texas. Louisiana was the only state in the very high category, according to the CDC’s Week 44 map.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
The CDC noted that an earlier increase in activity does not predict a higher seasonal peak or overall severity.

While it’s too early to know which flu viruses will be most dominant this season, in the week ending Nov. 7, the most frequently reported virus was influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, a descendant of the strain that caused the 2009 swine flu pandemic and has circulated seasonally since.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The CDC estimates that there have been 2.6 million illnesses, 36,000 hospitalizations and 2,100 deaths tied to flu infections so far this season. Five flu-associated deaths among children have been reported to the agency.
Cases of influenza are already on the rise across the U.S. this November. (iStock)
In an October media briefing, Dr. Anna Durbin of Johns Hopkins University stated that the flu hospitalization rate in mid-October was the highest it’s been in 15 years.
"Because the flu season is starting a bit earlier, I think it's really important for everyone to get a flu vaccine as soon as possible," she advised.

Dr. Fred Lopez, an infectious diseases specialist at the LSU Health Sciences Center in New Orleans, told the Associated Press that flu season is "taking off in a direction that’s only likely to increase in the next month or two."
"If you haven’t been vaccinated, you should get vaccinated now," he added.
The CDC recommends an annual seasonal flu vaccination, available for people 6 months and older. (iStock)

The CDC recommends an annual flu vaccine for everyone 6 months and older. Prescription antiviral drugs can treat flu and should be started as early as possible, especially for people at higher risk of complications.

With Thanksgiving approaching, doctors expect flu and other respiratory viruses to spread as people travel and gather with friends and family.
Last winter, flu activity surged in late December. At the time, New York City health officials described the season as the city’s most intense in 20 years, according to the AP.

title: Alzheimer’s blood marker could predict cognitive decline risks, Mayo Clinic says
summary: A Mayo Clinic study finds a p-tau217 blood test may predict cognitive decline risk within five to 10 years, offering a less invasive option than PET scans.
story: Clifford Jack Jr., a Mayo Clinic neuroradiologist, speaks about a blood test that detects a protein linked to Alzheimer’s disease, which could help predict whether older adults will develop cognitive decline within five to 10 years.

A blood test that detects a protein linked to Alzheimer’s disease could help predict whether older adults will develop cognitive decline within five to 10 years, according to a new Mayo Clinic study published in JAMA Neurology.

The study looked at levels of phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) in 2,178 cognitively unimpaired adults, ranging in age from 60 to 90. It also considered age, gender and whether participants carried the APOE ε4 genetic variant, which is associated with Alzheimer’s risk.
The participants, drawn from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, underwent blood biomarker testing, genetic testing and multiple cognitive assessments.
ALZHEIMER'S WARNING SIGNS COULD EMERGE YEARS BEFORE MEMORY LOSS, STUDY FINDS
While APOE ε4 had a modest association with risk after accounting for p-tau217, older age was associated with greater risk, according to the researchers.
For example, at the same elevated p-tau217 level, a 65-year-old faced a 6% estimated five-year risk of mild cognitive impairment, compared to a 37% risk for an 85-year-old.
A blood test that detects a protein linked to Alzheimer’s disease could help predict whether older adults will develop cognitive decline within five to 10 years. (iStock)
Alzheimer’s disease is marked by plaques and tangles that accumulate in the brain, senior author Clifford Jack Jr., a Mayo Clinic neuroradiologist, noted.

"The test tells you, just by taking a blood sample, whether someone has that pathology in the brain," he told Fox News Digital, adding higher levels of the pathology are associated with a greater risk of progressing from normal cognition to impairment.
10 HEALTH CONDITIONS MAY BE LINKED TO ALZHEIMER'S YEARS BEFORE DIAGNOSIS

Detecting p-tau217 in blood may be "less invasive and potentially more scalable" than using PET scans to measure amyloid burden, a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease that is associated with future cognitive impairment.

"The goal is to provide a personalized estimate of the risk of developing cognitive impairment that is more meaningful than simply reporting whether a blood test is positive or negative for amyloid pathology," first author Alicia Algeciras-Schimnich, Ph.D., a Mayo Clinic laboratory medicine and pathology researcher, said in a news release.
Alzheimer’s disease is marked by plaques and tangles that accumulate in the brain. (iStock)
If investigational treatments are found to be effective at preventing or delaying cognitive decline, this blood test could take on greater significance, according to the researchers.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"If preventive treatments become available, this kind of information could help patients and clinicians have more informed conversations about the potential benefits and risks of treatment," Jack noted.
Study limitations
The risk estimates were developed in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, which is drawn from a specific geographical area.
"The older population in southeast Minnesota is not representative of the entire United States," Jack said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
While the study’s methods could be applied to other populations, the researcher said the findings need to be replicated outside the region.
The study does not establish that routine blood testing prevents dementia or improves clinical outcomes. (iStock)
The risk prediction model is not yet ready for routine screening of people without cognitive symptoms, according to the research team.

"There is no treatment that’s been approved for people who are [asymptomatic] but have the disease in the brain," Jack told Fox News Digital. "Therefore, there’s no reason to do the test. … The results of the test would not change your medical management at all since there’s no treatment available."
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
That could change if preventive treatments are approved, he added.
The study does not establish that routine blood testing prevents dementia or improves clinical outcomes.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Many elderly people who have the pathology in the brain at lower levels will never develop symptoms in their lifetime," Jack added, noting that some people with Alzheimer’s-related pathology may also die of another cause before developing cognitive impairment.
