"They are very willing to lend a hand because they know it's a structural problem for our country," he added.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: Trump ally Bill Essayli tapped to lead investigation of Biden officials over Mar-a-Lago raid
summary: Bill Essayli will probe whether Biden officials broke the law in the FBI's 2022 raid on Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate, which sparked Jack Smith's case.
story: First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli breaks down the DOJ’s evidence of voter inconsistencies in California on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’
A California federal prosecutor embroiled in a legal battle over his own authority is heading to Florida to investigate the FBI’s 2022 raid on President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate.

Two sources familiar with the investigation confirmed to Fox News Digital that First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli will serve as a special assistant tasked with investigating whether Biden Justice Department officials broke federal law when executing their search warrant on Mar-a-Lago. Essayli will continue to hold his position as first assistant U.S. attorney, splitting his time between Florida and Los Angeles, a source familiar said.
Essayli’s inquiry into the Mar-a-Lago search, which initiated former special counsel Jack Smith’s classified documents case, is a part of a broader Justice Department probe.

Attorney General Pam Bondi initially launched the "grand conspiracy" investigation in August 2025 to target Obama-era officials, but its scope has since expanded to examine allegations that Biden officials also conspired to unlawfully prosecute Trump.

Essayli is the latest prosecutor tapped to oversee the investigation after the resignations of two other attorneys in the past few months. Just a few weeks ago, Jason Reding Quiñones, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, resigned abruptly. His departure came two months after he took over from Joe diGenova, a lawyer selected by Attorney General Todd Blanche to supervise the investigation who resigned in September.
PROSECUTOR JOSEPH DIGENOVA RESIGNS FROM DOJ ROLE INVESTIGATING TRUMP-RUSSIA PROBES

First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli leaves a news conference in Los Angeles Aug. 13, 2026. Essayli has been tapped to investigate whether Biden Justice Department officials broke federal law during the 2022 FBI raid on Mar-a-Lago. (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

DiGenova's resignation in September came just five months after he was tapped to oversee the investigation amid growing frustration within the White House and Justice Department over the lack of criminal charges. Fox News Digital previously reported that diGenova had effectively been sidelined before his departure, while sources told the New York Post he had lost the confidence of administration officials over concerns he was "slow-rolling" indictments and pursuing dead-end leads.
Essayli's involvement in the inquiry adds another layer of controversy to the investigation for two reasons.
TRUMP-FIRED US ATTORNEY LAUNCHES UNPRECEDENTED COURT FIGHT AFTER JUST 54 MINUTES ON THE JOB

President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach, Fla., on Nov. 26, 2024. The FBI's 2022 search of the property is the focus of a newly reassigned Justice Department investigation. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

For one, Essayli's authority to lead the U.S. Attorney's Office in Los Angeles is already under judicial scrutiny. In October, U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright ruled that Essayli was unlawfully serving as a "de facto" U.S. attorney, finding that the Justice Department had effectively circumvented restrictions on temporary appointments by allowing him to continue exercising the powers of the office without Senate confirmation.

Essayli was initially appointed interim U.S. attorney in April 2025, a position generally limited to 120 days. When that period expired, the Justice Department appointed him to other positions, including first assistant U.S. attorney, while allowing him to continue overseeing the office.

Seabright concluded that changing Essayli's title did not resolve the underlying legal problem and disqualified him from supervising two criminal prosecutions. On Monday, the judge rejected the Justice Department's request to suspend that ruling while the government pursued an appeal.

President Donald Trump speaks to reporters upon arriving at Glasgow Prestwick Airport in Prestwick, Scotland, on July 25, 2025. Trump's Justice Department has tapped California federal prosecutor Bill Essayli to lead its probe into the 2022 Mar-a-Lago search. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

Although that decision does not automatically invalidate Essayli's separate assignment in Florida, it raises questions about his continuing authority in Los Angeles as he takes on another politically sensitive investigation.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Essayli's close ties to Trump have also drawn scrutiny from Democrats and defense attorneys over whether he can remain impartial in an investigation involving the president's political adversaries.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

A former Republican California state lawmaker and vocal Trump supporter, Essayli has pledged to work "tirelessly" to carry out the administration's priorities at the Justice Department, prompting House Democrats led by Rep. Dave Min, D-Calif., to demand an ethics probe over alleged "politically-motivated investigations."

Meanwhile, H. Dean Steward, a veteran Newport Beach federal defense attorney and former directing attorney of the Orange County Federal Public Defender Office who successfully challenged Essayli's authority in California, has accused the Trump administration of violating federal law "in an effort to install minions as chief federal prosecutors."
Fox News Digital reached out to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California for comment but did not immediately receive a response.
Fox News' Jake Gibson and David Spunt contributed to this report.
Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

title: Americans could face $100 hike in internet bills under plan eyed by lawmakers
summary: Sens. Deb Fischer and Ben Ray Luján drafted a bill that would add up to $100 to people's internet bills to fund the Universal Service Fund.
story: The Internet & Television Association (NCTA) CEO Cory Gardner, a former U.S. Senator, tells Fox News Digital why Wi-Fi is "at risk" in America.
FIRST ON FOX: A bipartisan group of lawmakers is eyeing adding a tax to internet usage throughout the country to help subsidize telecommunications services in rural areas.

Sens. Deb Fischer, R-Neb., and Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., have quietly been working on draft legislation that would add up to $100 extra on Americans’ internet bills to bolster the Universal Service Fund (USF), a decades-old program meant to subsidize broadband access, a source shared with Fox News Digital.

Fischer and Luján formed a bipartisan and bicameral working group for USF reform last year with Reps. Doris Matsui, D-Calif., and Richard Hudson, R-N.C. to find fixes for the program, which was first launched in 1996.
FCC LAUNCHES SWEEPING REVIEW OF $3B SCHOOL INTERNET SUBSIDY PROGRAM OVER SCREEN TIME CONCERNS
Lawmakers are eyeing an internet usage tax to help subsidize telecommunications services in rural areas. (Carmen Jaspersen/picture alliance via Getty Images)

The draft legislation, which has yet to be officially filed in the Senate and is still subject to change, included proposals to create a USF tax on households and businesses with broadband connections. The draft legislation, which was reviewed by Fox News Digital, would also increase the current USF tax on cell phone lines and impose no cap on USF spending — meaning there’s wiggle room to raise the tax down the line.
"I’m not commenting on gossip intended to undermine USF reform, particularly when a bill hasn’t even been filed," Fischer said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
Another source familiar with the negotiations around the yet-to-be revealed legislation told Fox News Digital that they had "no reason to believe" that the fee had been removed from the draft bill.
"My understanding is it just adds a tax on broadband," they said.

Luján's office told Fox News Digital that discussions were still ongoing, that the "bipartisan working group continues to evaluate options to modernize the Universal Service Fund, ensure its long-term sustainability, and keep internet and communications services affordable for all Americans."
"No proposal has been finalized, and any claims otherwise are premature," they said.
Congress does not directly fund the program, which instead relies on user fees from telecommunications and broadband companies to stay afloat in order to subsidize broadband services in rural areas.
FCC CHAIRMAN CARR SAYS SPECTRUM AUCTION WILL MAKE WIRELESS FASTER, CHEAPER WHILE RAISING BILLIONS FOR TREASURY
Last year, according to data from the Congressional Research Service, the USF doled out over $8 billion in subsidies.
Part of the problem with the program is that the stream of funding that props USF up is shrinking, according to a report from the Computer & Communications Industry Association.

The report found that "the current contribution base for USF fell 41% between the first quarter of 2018 and the first quarter of 2026, from $12.9 billion to $7.6 billion." That is spurred by shifts in the industry and contribution base, like more communications happening over the internet through WhatsApp, FaceTime and Zoom instead of phone calls, for example.
And tacking on a new tax to bolster the program is a touchy subject, particularly for outside groups.
TOP SENATE DEM’S NEW TAX IDEA GETS TORCHED AS CRITICS WARN NEARLY EVERY AMERICAN COULD PAY
Chair Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Neb., gavels to order the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch hearing on April 15, 2026. (CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

Over two dozen outside groups led by Grover Norquist’s Americans for Tax Reform demanded in a letter to Congress sent in August that lawmakers "oppose any attempts to impose new taxes on broadband service, including by assessing broadband for contributions" to the USF.

"Rather than impose new taxes on broadband providers, raising costs yet further for consumers, Congress should reform eligibility for the program and retire the broadband subsidies, if not the entire program," they wrote. "USF is outdated and ill-suited for its purpose. Passing off its ballooning costs is not a solution."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Congress did enact a new infrastructure-expansion focused internet program under former President Joe Biden in 2021 as part of his Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.
That program, called the Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD), included a one-time pot of just over $42 billion to spread internet access across the country.
The Trump administration overhauled the program, removing hurdles and adding new guidelines for states and territories to gain access to the funding.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Dems, GOP rebels fail to rein in Trump's Iran war in Senate, but bigger battle looms
summary: Senate Democrats and rebel Republicans fail to pass a war powers resolution over Trump's Iran war, as Tim Kaine denies Republican shutdown threats.
story: Senate Majority Leader John Thune warns Democrats that attempting to shut down the government over military funding will backfire on them. He emphasizes that national security remains a top priority for the American people.
Senate Democrats failed to peel off enough Republicans to rebuke President Donald Trump and his war against Iran as another battle looms on the horizon.

In the first attempt after the midterm elections, Democrats and the squadron of rebel Republicans, including Sens. Susan Collins, R-Maine, Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, and Rand Paul, R-Ky., were not enough to pass a non-binding resolution that originally passed the House, pushed by Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., in September.

Like the previous war powers resolutions, this effort would have required the removal of troops engaged in hostilities not authorized by Congress in the region. Even if it had passed, it was a more symbolic move given that it was non-binding and would not have been sent to Trump’s desk.
DEMOCRATS COULD ENTER CONGRESSIONAL MAJORITY IN A GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN
Sen. Chuck Schumer said President Donald Trump, seen on Oct. 28, 2026, would be the subject of Senate investigations if he violates the law. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
But in the background, Senate Democrats are eyeing another battleground to be more forceful with their desire to rein in the war: government funding.

The deadline to either fully fund or extend current funding is Dec. 11. Senate Republicans have warned that their counterparts intend to use the process as a cudgel to stymie tax dollars meant for the war and are willing to shut down the government to do so.

"I'm increasingly concerned that the Democrats may try to initiate another, a third government shutdown this year," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said. "And that would be a terrible outcome for the American people and something I hope that they will think better of."
CHRIS VAN HOLLEN FLOATS USING GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN THREAT TO FORCE TRUMP TO END IRAN WAR

Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., countered to Fox News Digital that Senate Republicans were the ones who wanted to "shut the government down to maintain an illegal war that has just been massively repudiated by the American public."

"We're gonna fund government in a robust way. We're gonna fund the defense in a robust way, but if they say, ‘Yeah, that's not enough, we have to be able to continue a war that's illegal, and the American public hates,’ that'll be on them, not on us," Kaine said. "We're not gonna shut government down."

Thune’s comments came as Republicans were, until Wednesday afternoon, considering taking defense funding off the table and ramming a $350 billion request from the administration through with the budget reconciliation process.
But after a marathon closed-door meeting with Deputy Secretary of Defense Steve Feinberg, Republicans opted to give a shot at bipartisanship.
SENATE REPUBLICANS PLAN 54-DAY BLITZ TO PUSH TRUMP'S AGENDA BEFORE DEMOCRATS SEIZE POWER
Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., plans to force a vote on his war powers resolution to rein in President Donald Trump's military action in Iran. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"I think the consensus of the conference is, you know, there are downsides to reconciliation," Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said. "We're not giving up by any means, but we would like to give Democrats a chance to work through an appropriations process, defense supplemental, that kind of stuff."

Senate Democrats acknowledged that they’re in a hard spot when it comes to the funding back and forth, with some recognizing that they need to agree to funding the Pentagon and restocking munitions while struggling to find the balancing act on guardrails against taxpayer dollars flowing to the war effort.

"We're in a really tough place," Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., said. "I've been saying for months that the war with Iran has no support in my caucus. We are searching for responsible ways to bring it to an end, and a supplemental is a nonstarter, a reconciliation bill is a nonstarter, but I recognize we also need to find ways to invest in and support our troops and our security."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Republicans are also cautiously optimistic that Democrats will play ball, given the recent history with two record-shattering government shutdowns.

Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., was more optimistic than some of his colleagues, and told Fox News Digital that "I've got a lot of Democrat friends, both on the Armed Services Committee, who are, who are very supportive of our military. [They] understand the threat in the world."

"You know, they may have to, they may have to swallow their ‘I hate Trump pride’ a little bit, but, at the end of the day, there are a lot of people that are convincible," Cramer said. "But it does require talking to them. You know?"
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Wife of American wrongfully detained in China calls for his release after Trump-Xi meeting
summary: Sylvia Zin says her U.S. citizen husband Min Zin is held in solitary confinement in China without legal counsel, after Trump met with Xi Jinping again.
story: Wives of Americans wrongfully detained in China appeal for their husbands' release ahead of the high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Gillian Turner reports on the families of Youlin Chen and Min Zin as they share their emotional struggles and express hope for diplomatic intervention during bilateral discussions.

The wife of U.S. citizen Min Zin, whom the State Department has declared "wrongfully detained" in China, issued a fresh call for his release Thursday after President Donald Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
"It has now been nearly six months since my husband, Min Zin, a United States citizen and independent academic, was lured to China and wrongfully detained," Sylvia Zin said in a statement.

"My husband is being held by the Chinese government on false charges at an undisclosed location in solitary confinement without any access to legal counsel," she added. "We have no idea why they detained him and why they continue to hold him."

"This is the second in-person meeting that President Trump has held with Chinese President Xi since Min Zin was arrested. I am grateful for the President's commitment in continuing to raise my husband's wrongful detention and his work to secure Min Zin's immediate and unconditional release," Sylvia Zin also said. "My daughter and I remain hopeful in the President's ability to bring him home to us in time for the holidays."
TRUMP, PUTIN, XI ISSUE 4-POINT DECLARATION AFTER HISTORIC SUMMIT
Headshot of Min Zin.  (James W. Foley Legacy Foundation.)

When asked Thursday to respond to Sylvia Zin's statement, a White House official told Fox News Digital that Trump cares deeply about the return of Americans being held abroad and has brought home more than 100 from around the globe.

The State Department said in August that Secretary of State Marco Rubio determined Zin was "wrongfully detained" following an extensive review "of the circumstances surrounding his June 3 detention in Yunnan, China, where Mr. Zin had traveled to attend an academic conference at the invitation of the Chinese government."
TRUMP TO ASK XI TO FREE WRONGFULLY DETAINED US CITIZEN AS WIFE SPEAKS OUT
President Donald Trump walks with Chinese President Xi Jinping to their luncheon at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (Mark Schiefelbein/AP)

"There are now two wrongfully detained U.S. citizens in China: Mr. Zin and Dr. Youlin Chen," Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson said at the time. "The safety and security of U.S. citizens is the State Department’s top priority. We will continue to advocate for Mr. Zin and call for the release of all U.S. citizens who are arbitrarily detained or exit-banned in China."
China's Foreign Ministry claimed Zin was arrested in June on suspicion of spying and endangering national security, according to Reuters.
The Institute for Strategy and Policy-Myanmar think tank said Zin is its director, and The Associated Press reported in June that Zin was a Ph.D. candidate at the University of California, Berkeley.

Sylvia Zin also said in her statement, "We recently learned that Min Zin was hospitalized last month for severe dehydration due to stomach illness and that there is no heat in the location he is being held.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"I try to remain strong for our daughter," she added, "but my worry for my husband's health and well-being grows unbearably with each passing day."
Fox News' Nicholas Kalman and Stephen Sorace contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Florida Christians rebel against Imam's prayer opening a city meeting with a message of their own
summary: Christian protesters reciting the Lord's Prayer interrupted Imam Sajid Bhuiya's invocation at a Bartow, Florida meeting before police stepped in.
story: A group of Floridians showed up to a city commission meeting in the town of Bartow to protest an Imam’s invocation, praying the Lord’s Prayer in response to the Imam’s invitation. (Credit: Citizens Defending Freedom)

An imam who was scheduled to deliver the invocation at a city commission meeting Monday evening in a southwest Florida town was interrupted by Christian protesters — who had a prayer of their own to share.

Footage from inside the meeting obtained by Fox News Digital shows dozens of Christian activists crowded into the back of a Bartow, Florida city commission meeting room. As Imam Sajid Bhuiya of the town's Masjid Al-Nur Mosque stepped up to the lectern to give the invocation, they began reciting the Lord's Prayer in unison. Some chants of "USA!" broke out, as well.

According to Robert Goodman, the southeast regional director of the conservative activist group Citizens Defending Freedom, news of Bhuiya's scheduled appearance began making the rounds on social media last weekend. He was among those who shared the news on social media. Goodman said about 100 people from different groups ended up attending the meeting.
IOWA CITY COUNCIL MEETING ERUPTS AFTER FORMER MEMBER OPENS WITH SATANIC PRAYER AND 'HAIL SATAN'
Christian protesters pack a city commission meeting in Bartow, Florida, as a local imam attempts to deliver the invocation. (Citizens Defending Freedom)

"Citizens Defending Freedom believes Christian voices deserve to be heard on matters affecting our communities, families, and freedoms, which is why we joined many other concerned citizens and organizations Monday night," Goodman told Fox News Digital.
He said the Quran teaches forced submission and permits men to strike their wives, while viewing the opinions of women as lesser than the opinions of men.

"We have every right to challenge teachings we believe conflict with human dignity, equality, religious liberty and America's founding principles, because we must be intolerant of intolerance while respecting every person's right to believe differently," he said.
Video from the city's official livestream of the event quickly went viral online.
PASTOR UNLEASHES ON DEARBORN AS RELIGIOUS TENSIONS ERUPT AT CITY COUNCIL MEETING: 'ENOUGH IS ENOUGH'
Some protesters made off-color comments, including telling Bhuiya to go back to his own country, which Goodman clarified that neither he nor his organization support.

"The disrespectful remarks made by two or three individuals Monday night do not represent me or Citizens Defending Freedom, because as Christians, we are called to speak truth with conviction and respect, not insults," Goodman said.
Goodman said Bhuiya was invited to deliver the invocation by a city official. Members of the commission mostly sat quietly, observing the commotion while police handled the crowd.
Police eventually escorted the Christian protesters out of the building, though no arrests were made.
Imam Sajid Bhuiya of Masjid Al-Nur Mosque delivering the invocation at a Bartow, Florida city commission meeting after being interrupted by Christian protesters. (Robert Goodman)

Bhuiya then spoke, quoting passages from the Quran that he said are meant to unify people. "This is a reminder that our differences in background, culture and faiths should not prevent us from treating one another with dignity," he said.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Masjid Al-Nur Mosque for comment on the disruption of Bhuiya's invocation.
SWING STATE MAYOR SUED AS CITY’S MUSLIM HOLIDAY DISPLAYS IGNITE RELIGIOUS-FAVORITISM FIGHT
The city of Bartow released a statement explaining the Imam's appearance at the meeting.
The statement said that residents, "joined by individuals from other cities, attempted to prevent the imam from speaking and the Mayor from proceeding to conduct the business at hand."
A holy Christian cross laying on an open Bible with an American flag in the background. (iStock)

"For years, it has been tradition to open Bartow City Commission meetings with a prayer offered by either a faith-based leader or one of the City's elected officials," it said. "While historically the opening invocation/prayer is one based on Christian traditions, the opportunity is open to all faiths. This is consistent with the United States Constitution."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In the statement, city officials called for residents, "including religious leaders of all faiths, to come together to ensure that Bartow continues to be a welcoming place for all who live, work and play in Polk County's capital city."
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: ‘Long term coup’ ousted Christians, conservatives from major watchdog, insider claims
summary: A former SPLC director told FBI agents Christians and conservatives were pushed out first in what he called a "long-term coup" at the Southern Poverty Law Center.
story: Former Southern Poverty Law Center executive Heidi Beirich faces federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy. The Department of Justice alleges Beirich hid over $4 million in payments from SPLC donors to fund White supremacy.

A former Southern Poverty Law Center official who led its hate-group tracking work told FBI agents he tried to make the watchdog’s controversial "Hate Map" more ideologically balanced, while saying Christians and conservatives were the first staffers pushed out in what he called a "long-term coup" at the organization after he left in 2013.

The former director said he pushed for a more evenhanded SPLC, arguing that its "Hate Map" — which lists conservative groups alongside Ku Klux Klan chapters — should also include left-wing extremists, including violent animal-rights and extremist environmental groups. However, the former director said the effort met resistance and that, as liberal leaders reshaped the organization, most of his 17-person team was replaced.

"There was some kind of coup, long-term coup going on there between some, what I would — what I heard were some pretty liberal people, extreme people that had other ideas about what we were doing," the unnamed former director told agents, as first reported by The Daily Signal's Tyler O'Neil, who has been covering the SPLC's legal troubles.
DOJ EXPANDS INDICTMENT AGAINST SPLC, ALLEGING $4M SECRETLY FUNNELED TO KKK AND EXTREMIST GROUPS
SPLC Intelligence Project Director Heidi Beirich speaks during an event on Jan. 12, 2018. (David Buchan/Variety/Penske Media via Getty Images)

The former director’s comments appeared in an FBI interview transcript filed as an exhibit to Dr. Heidi Beirich’s Nov. 2 court filing. Beirich, a former SPLC official charged alongside the organization in a federal case alleging a scheme to mislead donors and banks about donations used to pay informants associated with violent extremist groups, pointed to multiple FBI interviews with an unnamed former SPLC director, identified in the filing as "Individual-1."

In a January interview, Individual-1 told investigators he ran the SPLC’s field-source program, set up accounts used to pay sources and directed payments, according to Beirich’s filing. During a March 23 follow-up interview with Individual-1, FBI Special Agents David McDaniel and Parker Still framed the conversation around the program having "gone off the rails" under Beirich and told the former director they were not there to discuss the bank activity, noting he had "obviously nothing to do with all that," before questioning him about the SPLC’s alleged targeting of conservative organizations and Beirich’s role, according to the transcript.
EXCLUSIVE: SPLC'S 'FAR-LEFT,' 'ANTI-RACISM' CURRICULUM FOUND IN CLASSROOMS AS EARLY AS KINDERGARTEN: 'WATCHDOG'

Individual-1 responded that, as his "gut impression," he believed her actions were political and accused some liberals at the center of having "a good degree of hatred" for conservatism, according to the March 23 transcript.

Individual-1 also alleged a shift in power at the SPLC. After he left in 2013, he said, people were appointed to the SPLC’s board as "figureheads" and eventually gained enough voting power to take over the center. He said only one or two data-entry members of his roughly 17-person team remained, with the others replaced by staff he believed shared the new leadership’s politics.

"That's who they ran off first were the Christians and conservatives," the unnamed former director told agents when asked why Beirich took the actions she did after his departure. "Then they — then the rest they just replaced with people they liked, you know, that agreed with them politically."
HOW MUTINY AT SOUTHERN POVERTY LAW CENTER TRIGGERED LEADERSHIP COLLAPSE
The Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) building seen in March 2020 in Montgomery, Alabama. (Barry Lewis/InPictures via Getty Images)

In separate comments about the SPLC's controversial "Hate Map," Individual-1 said he persuaded SPLC staff, despite internal resistance, to list Black separatist groups, which he considered comparable to White racist groups, on the map. However, he said he unsuccessfully pushed the SPLC to include violent animal-rights and environmental extremist groups and described his team’s approach during his tenure as director as "very nonpartisan" and "middle of the road."
"We were very nonpartisan, or at least when I was running things, when I was director, we stayed right in the middle of the road," he said.

In a June follow-up, the unnamed former director also criticized the SPLC's "Hate Map" for listing local chapters separately, saying it made the map's totals of the extremist groups it chose to identify look larger.
WATCH: SPLC CHIEF DOUBLES DOWN ON PLACING CHARLIE KIRK'S TURNING POINT USA ON 'HATE MAP'

While the unnamed former director was not charged in the SPLC case, Beirich was. Her lawyers say the interviews with the unnamed director warrant discovery into whether she was singled out because of her perceived role in the SPLC’s political speech, arguing that investigators’ questions about the SPLC’s treatment of conservative groups — and her alleged role in that work — could show the prosecution was motivated by hostility to the center’s political speech.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Individual-1’s statements confirm my longstanding criticism of the Southern Poverty Law Center, that it exaggerates ‘hate’ by inflating the chapters on its ‘hate map’ and that it systematically demonizes conservatives and Christians while turning a blind eye to extremism on the Left," O’Neil, the author of "Making Hate Pay: The Corruption of the Southern Poverty Law Center," told Fox News Digital. "Now, we have the former director of the Intelligence Project saying the SPLC appears to have pushed out Christians and conservatives, while rejecting his suggestion to include environmentalist agitators on the map."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Fox News Digital reached out to the SPLC and attorneys for Heidi Beirich for comment but did not receive a response in time for publication.
Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: Hometown of accused US military plane saboteur is a known magnet for anti-Israel activism
summary: Cork, Ireland, hometown of Daithí O’Corráin, who faces U.S. charges of destroying a $60 million C-130, once banned Benjamin Netanyahu from its city limits.
story: Two people were arrested by Irish police after agitators gathered at Trinity College Dublin while former President Joe Biden made a surprise visit on Tuesday (Credit: Credit: PA Media via Reuters).
The European hometown of the man who single-handedly destroyed a U.S. military transport aircraft in an act of apparent protest has a rich history of pro-Palestinian support.

This includes the town council for Cork, Ireland, barring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from entering its city limits, citing his "illegal occupation of Palestine and bordering countries" and the continuous pro-Palestinian protests taking place every Saturday since October 2023, organized by the Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign (CPSC).

Cork’s opposition to Israel adds context to the possible motives for why Daithí O’Corráin, an Irish national, allegedly destroyed a U.S. military C-130 Hercules aircraft in April. The incident also draws attention to several anti-Israel groups that have sprung up in Ireland in recent years.
IRELAND’S ELITES HAVE FOUND THEIR NEW RELIGION: HATING ISRAEL

Pro-Palestinian activists from the Ireland Palestine Solidarity Campaign, supported by members of left-wing parties including People Before Profit and the Socialist Party and students, participate in the National March for Palestine from the Garden of Remembrance to O'Connell Street and Leinster House, on May 18, 2024, in Dublin, Ireland. (Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Ireland’s anti-Israel foothold became international news in April when O’Corráin, a Cork native, barricaded himself inside a C-130, a U.S. military transport plane. Once inside, he tore out critical wiring, destroyed gauges, contaminated fuel tanks and even poured corrosive chemicals into the aircraft, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.
Although his motives remain unclear, several groups from Cork interpreted his actions as a form of resistance against Israel and U.S. military interventionism.

In one such case, a Cork business owner named Tracey Ryan launched an initiative to raise €20,000 for O’Corráin's legal defense, praising his efforts to resist "the unwanted presence of U.S. military in Ireland in the face of their illegal war & support of Israel’s genocide."

"We, Daithí's friends and comrades, are raising funds to support him through his court case. We would really appreciate your support & will keep you updated here on ways to support Daithí," Ryan wrote in the description of the fundraising page.

According to her personal Facebook profile, Ryan joined a bus of pro-Palestinian activists who went to support O’Corráin at his court appearance. "Bus going to the high court to support Daithí on Thursday!!" Ryan wrote.
O’Corráin has also received support from CPSC, the Cork pro-Palestinian group.

As news of the incident spread, CPSC co-chair Anne McShane posted on her Palestinian advocacy Facebook page in support of O’Corráin, encouraging viewers to send him letters of encouragement after his incarceration.
"Daithi needs our support in order to keep up his morale. Letters are a lifeline for prisoners," an April 17 post read.

CPSC spearheads anti-Israel demonstrations in Cork. In addition to hosting several pro-Palestinian fundraising initiatives, the group facilitates weekly Saturday demonstrations and invites speakers. At one point, CPSC’s website featured a fundraising site for O’Corráin, but the page has since been removed.
INSIDE THE PROTEST PLAYBOOK TO VILIFY ISRAEL ON 'GLOBAL DAY OF ACTION'

Left: Smashed cockpit instruments inside a U.S. military C-130H Hercules aircraft allegedly destroyed at Shannon Airport in Ireland on April 11, 2026. Right: A separate U.S. Air Force C-130 Hercules aircraft at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England, on March 18, 2026. (U.S. Department of Justice; Leon Neal/Getty Images)
In CPSC’s own words, the group is part of a larger pro-Palestinian movement.

"It’s not just the city. Towns across all of County Cork stand in solidarity with Palestinians, including Ballincollig, Bandon, Cobh, Charleville, Clonakilty, Fermoy, Kinsale, Macroom, Mallow, Mitchelstown, Skibbereen and more," the group states on its website.
"Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign is a branch of the Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign (IPSC)," it added.

As part of its sister groups’ efforts "to foster links between Palestine and Irish institutions and organizations," CPSC and IPSC have both applauded Cork’s city council efforts to promote pro-Palestinian policies.
"Well done to the Cork City Council which passed a motion … calling for the Central Bank to end the sale of Israeli bonds," one Facebook post reads.
The groups have also held Cork up as a template for Ireland’s national policy.

"We call on the Irish government to follow the example of both Dublin and Cork city councils by officially recognizing Israeli Apartheid – and acting to end any and all links to this regime," another statement reads.

For its own part, the Cork City Council has earned the support of IPSC and CPSC through a range of its official resolutions, making the town’s formal position to condemn any of Ireland’s ties to Israel.

In addition to banning Netanyahu from entering the city's limits in a 41-8 vote in 2024, Cork’s council has flown the Palestinian flag over city hall on U.N. International Day of Solidarity and called on Ireland to ban trade from Israeli settlements.
Cork has even passed a "twinning" mechanism with the Palestinian city of Nablus — a largely symbolic partnership.
IRISH PM REJECTS ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS IN IRELAND AMID DRAMATIC VOTE OVER BOYCOTTING ISRAEL GAME

Conoe Kelliher from Ballyvourney holds a Palestinian flag whilst attending a watch-along party in the town square of Ireland's Eurovision entrant Bambie Thug's hometown of Macroom in Co Cork, as the Eurovision final takes place at Malmo Arena on Saturday, May 11, 2024. (Noel Sweeney/PA Images via Getty Images)

Fergal Dennehy, the lord mayor of Cork from 2025 to 2026, hosted the mayor of Nablus in February, calling the partnership "just the beginning of what we hope will be a wonderful relationship between our two great cities."
Neither CPSC nor Cork City Council responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment on the city's pro-Palestinian positions or about connections to O’Corráin.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
O’Corráin is incarcerated in Ireland and faces criminal charges in the U.S. for "destruction of government property," valued at $60 million.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: AOC leaves door open to 2028 presidential run, signals willingness to work with Trump
summary: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez would not rule out a 2028 White House run, saying her focus is getting results for people after Democrats reclaimed the House majority.
story: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., told Fox News Digital she hopes to work with President Donald Trump on a stock trading ban and healthcare, while leaving the door open to a potential presidential run.
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is leaving the door open to a potential 2028 presidential bid as speculation grows over her political future.
"I think, right now, this election just happened. We got to work on getting results for people," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital when asked whether she was considering a presidential run in 2028.

The self-described democratic socialist also expressed a willingness to work with President Donald Trump on key legislative priorities as Democrats prepare to take control of the House following the 2026 midterm elections.
PROGRESSIVE ORG LAUNCHES CAMPAIGN URGING AOC TO RUN FOR PRESIDENT WHILE PROGRESSIVES EYE SOCIALIST CANDIDATE

Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Laurel Lee, R-Fla., and Kat Cammack, R-Fla., hold a news conference with media personality Paris Hilton urging Congress to pass the DEFIANCE Act (Disrupt Explicit Forged Images and Non-Consensual Edits Act) outside the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 17, 2026. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)

Ocasio-Cortez, who has drawn support from the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) New York City chapter for a potential White House bid, emphasized her desire to advance legislation in the 120th Congress rather than focus on presidential politics.
Asked whether Democrats should work with Trump instead of prioritizing impeachment proceedings and congressional investigations, Ocasio-Cortez expressed optimism about finding common ground.
"I hope so," she told Fox News Digital.
"You know, I hope that President Trump can sign a congressional stock trading ban into law," Ocasio-Cortez continued.

The congresswoman also identified healthcare reform as a potential area for bipartisan cooperation, urging Trump to address changes to Medicaid that she warned could threaten coverage for millions of Americans.
DOZENS OF HOUSE DEMOCRATS REJECT BILL FUSING CONGRESSIONAL STOCK BAN WITH FEDERAL VOTER ID
President Donald Trump speaks in the James Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House on Nov. 9, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Alex Brandon/AP Photo)

"I hope President Trump will be willing to work with us in really adjusting this Medicaid and confronting this Medicaid cliff that stands to kick off millions of working Americans off of their healthcare," she said.
"And so, you know, there are going to be areas where we're going to have real disagreement and real confrontation or worse," she continued.
Despite those disagreements, Ocasio-Cortez argued that lawmakers should prioritize legislation addressing Americans' immediate concerns.
"My hope is that we can prioritize the things that can actually change people's lives for the better as quickly as possible," she said.
Her remarks came hours after House Democrats overwhelmingly nominated Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., for speaker of the 120th Congress.

At least five of the 11 Democrats who opposed Jeffries’ nomination are incoming Congress members and self-described democratic socialists who argued that the party's leadership does not adequately represent their political priorities.
JEFFRIES SURVIVES DEM VOTE TO SECURE SPEAKER POSITION AS PROGRESSIVE RESISTANCE CLOUDS HIS CHANCES
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries speaks during a press conference on Capitol Hill on Nov. 3, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images)
Ocasio-Cortez, a DSA member, acknowledged that ideological disagreements between Jeffries and the party's socialist wing could continue throughout the next Congress.
"Of course, there are going to be areas where leader Jeffries and DSA are going to be in strong opposition," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
However, she expressed confidence that Democrats could unite around shared priorities, including expanding access to publicly funded healthcare.

Her comments highlight the competing pressures facing House Democrats as they prepare to govern with a new majority while balancing progressive policy demands, internal ideological divisions and potential opportunities to work with the Trump administration.
Jeffries did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: ASRA Q. NOMANI: Old-guard Dems face Frankenstein moment as leftists come for them
summary: Last Thursday, Ben Cohen and CodePink packed a House Longworth Building office demanding an end to the Iran war as activists turn on Democratic leaders.
story: Democrats cultivated far-left activist networks to mobilize voters and defeat Republicans. Now, a "red-green-green" alliance of socialist, anti-Israel and climate activists challenges party leaders.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Ice cream magnate Ben Cohen and activists from the far-left nonprofit CodePink packed into a lawmaker's office in House Longworth Building Room 1236 last week, demanding an end to the war in Iran, a cutoff of U.S. military ties to Israel and the removal of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth.

Next door, in House Rayburn Building Room 2267, Capitol police officers arrested far-left, anti-Israel demonstrators, including prolific street theater activist Hazami Barmada, cloaked in symbolic blood red, as they packed another lawmaker's office, condemning complicity in Israel's alleged "genocide" of Palestinians in Gaza.

Across Capitol Hill in Senate Hart Building Room 322, police officers arrested young adults from a far-left nonprofit and political action committee, Sunrise Movement, as they packed a senator's office, condemning his politics, including his support of Israel.
The next day, an activist from a far-left nonprofit, Climate Defiance, screamed at a high-ranking lawmaker speaking at a political conference, calling him a "traitor."
But they weren't going after Republican lawmakers.
They were far-left activists with a special target: The Democratic Party's leadership.
JEFFRIES BRUSHES OFF OPPOSITION FROM FAR-LEFT DEMS WHO VOTED NO: 'WE’RE GOING TO WORK TOGETHER'

The target of Cohen, the co-founder of Ben and Jerry's, was California Democratic Rep. Nancy Pelosi, former speaker of the House. The anti-Israel protesters had filled the office of Democratic Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, nominated Wednesday by fellow Democrats to be the next House speaker despite the protests.

The Sunrise Movement agitators had flooded the office of top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer, and the activists of Climate Defiance were attempting to shame Jeffries at a conference of the Democratic Party.

The groups protesting top Democrats represent the full spectrum of a "red-green-green-blue" alliance – made up of socialist and pro-communist "red" organizations, Muslim and Arab "green" groups, environmental "green" activists and traditional "blue" groups. The alliance has emerged in recent years to press a far-left agenda in U.S. politics, particularly on the issue of ending U.S. support for Israel.

A Fox News Digital investigation reveals that 22 groups from the network – harnessing about $342 million in annual revenues – are now waging a coordinated effort, dubbed "CHUCK CHUCK," aimed at ousting Schumer from his expected role as Senate majority leader, creating the myth of the marching millions with shared messaging, social media campaigns, influencer videos and staged arrests.

The campaign is operating on several fronts: activists "bird-dogging" lawmakers in the halls of Congress, national advocacy organizations endorsing Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen over Schumer, local chapters organizing demonstrations and supporters mobilizing phone calls to senators ahead of a Dec. 1 secret-ballot leadership election.

On Monday, Brooklyn activists from a traditionally Democratic group, Indivisible Project, plan to "celebrate" Schumer's 76th birthday with a protest against him at his Third Avenue midtown Manhattan office.
Schumer maintains that he has the votes to win, and he most likely does.
Members of the Sunrise Movement protest in Sen. Chuck Schumer's office in a staged disturbance on Nov. 12, 2026. (Sunrise Movement)

A Fox News Digital anti-Schumer tracker shows that Van Hollen only has the support of five sitting or incoming senators: Bernie Sanders, Abdul El-Sayed, Jeff Merkley, Peggy Flanagan and himself. But he does have 22 organizations fueling and amplifying the anti-Schumer campaign to win more votes. So far, they include:

5 (red) socialist and far-left groups: BreakThrough BT Media Inc.'s BreakThrough News, CodePink, Democratic Socialists of America Inc., Our Revolution and Working Families Organization Inc.;3 (green) Muslim, Arab and pro-Palestinian groups: U.S. Council of Muslim Organizations, Council on American-Islamic Relations and Bend the Arc: Jewish Action Inc.;3 (blue) labor unions: International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, National Nurses United and Office and Professional Employees International Union;2 (blue) Section 527 political organizations: Young Dems of Maryland and High School Democrats of America;8 (blue) Democratic-aligned organizations: 50501, Friends of USAID, FLARE USA, Indivisible Project, Indivisible Brooklyn, MoveOn.org Civic Action, Showing Up for Justice Inc. and Rise and Resist Inc.1 (green) environmental group: Sunrise Movement.

SCHUMER BOASTS EARLY ADVANTAGE IN SENATE POWER STRUGGLE AS DEM RIVAL WARNS AGAINST 'CORONATION'

The emerging dynamics are reminiscent of the Frankenstein story, with the Democratic establishment empowering the powerful activist movement to defeat its Republican opponents. But now, parts of that movement are turning on the very political establishment that helped bring them to power.
Earlier this year, the Sunrise Movement's executive director, Aru Shiney-Ajay, led an online discussion, published on YouTube, headlined "How to Take Over the Democratic Party."

Neera Tanden, a longtime ally of Bill and Hillary Clinton and now executive director of the Center for American Progress, a Democratic nonprofit created by former Clinton administration chief of staff John Podesta, has another term for the rebels from within who challenge Jeffries: "chaos agents."

On Tuesday, she wrote on X, "I personally would like the names of everyone who wins an historic election and then immediately goes into a circular firing squad so we can tag the chaos agents for the future."

Meanwhile, witnessing the targeting of Jeffries as a "traitor," Texas Democratic Party advisor Kurt Bardella wrote on X, "I can tell you there are times when the tactics and venom coming from the activist left are completely indistinguishable to the MAGA right. They just come off as unhinged a--holes who are throwing tantrums."
PROGRESSIVES FACE ACCUSATIONS OF RACISM OVER ATTACKS ON HAKEEM JEFFRIES AS HE SEEKS SPEAKERSHIP

When Code Pink co-founder Medea Benjamin emerged from Pelosi's office last week, trailing behind Capitol Police officers called by staffers to assess the situation, she told Fox News Digital: "See, we're bipartisan. We yell at Democrats as much as we yell and scream at Republicans."
Importantly, for some of them, the goal of the "red" in the red-green-green-blue alliance isn't Western free-enterprise democracy.
Benjamin's fellow CodePink co-founder, Jodie Evans, gave Fox News Digital a more ideological explanation for rejecting Democrats alongside Republicans, as she stood outside Pelosi's office.

"I'm a socialist, because I believe in equality, so I teach it. It's the peace economy," Evans said. "Socialism is the peace of economy. I read Marx to try to understand why we were at war with communists. Like, well, how bad were they?... They wanted equality for everyone! What insanity!"

The encounters last week captured a fault line running through the opposition to President Donald Trump. Some activists want to push the Democratic Party further left. Others who are openly pro-socialist and pro-communist reject both major parties and see a Democratic victory as another opportunity to organize against the political establishment.
QUIET PART OUT LOUD: ANTI-ISRAEL MOBS WANT ONE STATE CALLED 'PALESTINE,' ERASING ISRAEL
Most importantly, a connective thread runs through the protests by the "red-green-green-blue" alliance: anti-Israel messaging.

Within the broader pro-Palestinian movement, activists advocate different goals, including a Palestinian "right of return" to Israel, a single democratic "one state" encompassing Israel and the Palestinian territories, an end to "Zionism" and Israel's status as a Jewish state, and the emergence of a "free, free Palestine" "from the river to the sea."

Proponents of a "one-state" solution argue that Palestinians and their descendants displaced following Israel's creation in 1948 should be permitted the "right of return" and receive "equal rights" in Israel. Critics contend that such a demographic transformation would end Israel's character as a Jewish homeland. Supporters invoke "rules-based international law" to describe their proposals as a framework for "human rights," "equal rights" and "self-determination" for Palestinians.

These fissures with centrist Democrats are being expressed by the leaders of groups including CodePink, BreakThrough BT Media, the People's Forum and Tricontinental, funded by American-born communist tycoon Neville Roy Singham, who lives in Shanghai, supporting the Chinese Communist Party. CodePink's Evans is married to Singham. Congressional investigators and Justice Department prosecutors have investigated Singham's activities and funding as possible malign foreign influence. No charges have been filed against Singham or the groups he has funded.
SCHUMER'S LEADERSHIP RIVAL REVEALS MAJOR SENATE RULE CHANGE HE'D PURSUE IF ELECTED
Alex Soros has a critical perspective of Sunrise Movement over their stance of Palestinians, according to a recent interview. (Jason Alden/Bloomberg via Getty Images/Robert Gauthier/Getty Images)

Even with Jeffries' leadership survival, their targets include the two Democrats positioned to lead the incoming congressional Democratic majority – Schumer and Jeffries – with disputes over U.S. support for Israel among the grievances raised by activists interviewed by Fox News Digital.

The confrontations harken back to the protests surrounding the 2024 Democratic National Convention in Chicago, where demonstrators gathered at Union Park and marched toward the convention, denouncing Vice President Kamala Harris as "Killer Kamala" and President Joe Biden as "Genocide Joe" for supporting Israel in its campaign against Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel.
Some of the same organizations and activists challenging Democrats today were gathered in Union Park back then.
Two years later, Democrats’ midterm victories have brought another round of demands, demonstrations and threats to withhold support from Democratic Party leaders.

In an April 2025 interview with New York magazine, Alexander Soros, son of billionaire Democratic Party funder George Soros, expressed his frustration with the leftist environmentalist group Sunrise Movement, which has been heavily funded by Soros organizations.
"What the hell did they do, by the way?" Soros said in the interview. "We gave them money, and now all they do is talk about Palestine. It’s ridiculous."
ALEX SOROS FUMES AT LEFT-WING CLIMATE GROUP OVER 'PALESTINE' OBSESSION
The dynamics of the "chaos agents" ramped up even as votes were still being counted from the Democratic Party's "blue tsunami" wins in the midterm elections.

On Nov. 4, the day after the election, BreakThrough News host Rania Khalek, in D.C. last week for lobbying organized by CodePink, led a panel discussion with co-host Zoe Alexandra featuring the top Singham network personalities — BreakThrough News editor-in-chief Ben Becker; People's Forum executive director Manolo De Los Santos; and Tricontinental executive director Vijay Prashad — blasting the Democrats.
That day, the Democratic Socialists of America declared that voters had "emphatically endorsed socialism" and urged Americans to reject "the complacent center and the fascist right."

The next day, BreakThrough published a Khalek segment titled "Schumer & Jeffries reap the backlash to the genocide they enabled," accusing the Democratic leaders of benefiting politically from opposition to policies they had helped sustain.

Khalek followed the next day with a written appeal linking to her "BT Live" segment. She accused Democratic leaders of serving wealthy interests and argued that sustained organizing could force policy concessions.
"Do not go back to brunch. Get organized," she wrote.

Also on Nov. 5, Our Revolution, a 501(c)(4) political nonprofit backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, an elder statesman revered by members of the Democratic Socialists of America, made clear that its leadership challenge extended to both chambers. "Real question: how do people calling for Schumer to step down justify giving Hakeem Jeffries a pass?" the group posted.
By Saturday, Nov. 7, that pressure was visible on Manhattan’s streets.

Demonstrators marched from Times Square toward Seventh Avenue and 14th Street in a rally organized by groups including the Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter. The protests were cast as anti-Trump but there was another theme in the crowd: anti-Democratic Party.
Among their chants: "Jeffries, Schumer let’s be clear, ICE is not wanted here."
Demonstrators held signs reading, "Remove Jeffries / Schumer" and "CALL JEFFRIES & SCHUMER / TELL THEM TO STEP ASIDE."

One sign repeated the thread of anti-Israel activism, aimed also at the pro-Israel lobbying group, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee: "They are not capable of meeting this moment. We need FIGHTERS with BACKBONE & VISION – not corporate & AIPAC hacks."
By Sunday, Nov. 8, the Party for Socialism and Liberation, a communist group working out of the headquarters of the People's Forum on Wesr 37th Street in Manhattan, attacked Schumer directly.
"Chuck Schumer isn’t an ‘architect’ of anything except the genocide in Gaza," the organization wrote, adding that Schumer had no place leading a Senate "which should be abolished anyway."
CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE
Code Pink co-founders Jodie Evans and Medea Benjamin walk through office buildings on Capitol Hill to organize protests. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)
By early last week, the pressure campaign had reached Schumer’s and Jeffries' offices.
At 12:51 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10, CodePink's Benjamin tried to enter Schumer's office in Hart Room 322, and posted a video with the message: "Chuck Schumer locked his office on us!"
The next day, at 10:35 a.m., the activists reached Jeffries' office in Rayburn Room 2267 and Benjamin recorded a staged statement outside the door for CodePink's social media account.

On Thursday, Nov. 12, Barmada, wearing her red costume, joined a new confrontation at Jeffries’ office, filming as Capitol Police escorted other activists away. Iran's state-run Press TV later promoted the protest on its anti-U.S. propaganda platform. Barmada didn't respond to a request for comment.
Across the Capitol complex, at 2:55 p.m., Schumer's staff faced the sit-in staged by Sunrise Movement's protest organizers, chanting on script, "Hey hey, ho ho, Schumer has got to go!"
Capitol Police arrested 54 activists during the Sunrise Movement action, and a battalion of influencers splashed the news across social media in a series of similar posts.
ASRA NOMANI: EL-SAYED GLIDES INTO ROLE AS ROCK STAR OF THE HARD LEFT'S RED-GREEN ALLIANCE

By Thursday night, amid the coordinated campaign by the left, the campaign to replace Schumer had a declared candidate. Van Hollen announced he would seek the majority leader’s job, and El-Sayed endorsed him.
Just days earlier, El-Sayed had smiled quietly as the board president of the Arab America Foundation led a supportive crowd in chants of "Free, free Palestine," "from the river to the sea."

El-Sayed previously served on the board of the Sunrise Movement, whose organizers have been demanding Schumer's removal. The relationship illustrates how the pressure campaign extends beyond street demonstrations to elected Democrats with histories in activist organizations.

That day, Democratic Socialists of America published a message, "SAY NO TO SCHUMER," over images of the leader. Soon after, the "World Socialist Web Site," representing a pro-communist "world Trotskyist movement" and "Marxist world outlook," promoted the "SAY NO TO SCHUMER" campaign, touting Van Hollen as a "lifelong servant of the Democratic establishment."

The next day, CodePink's D.C. organizer, Olivia DiNucci, regularly seen heckling public officials and lawmakers, responded with a triumphant video, calling on activists to lobby against Schumer in the halls of Congress and flood congressional officials with the message: "VOTE CHRIS, NOT CHUCK."

And, wearing a hot pink T-shirt with the graphic of a watermelon, a quirky symbol of Palestinian "resistance," and "Falasteen," the Arabic word for a Palestinian homeland, CodePink's Benjamin responded that day by urging support for Van Hollen, citing as her first reason: "He has been a forceful critic of Israel's assault on Palestinians."

The campaign to oust Schumer is now drawing support from two of the Democratic Party’s most established "progressive" political nonprofits: Indivisible Project and MoveOn.org Civic Action, both 501(c)(4) nonprofits.

Indivisible Project says it opposes Schumer's "coronation," and Indivisible Brooklyn is promoting an "Even New Yorkers Don’t Want Chuck" week of action, including a Times Square rally on Thursday, co-sponsored by other Indivisible chapters.
MoveOn reports that 75% of participating members who voted support Van Hollen.

Meanwhile, last Friday, Barmada posted a video with one of the activists arrested at Jeffries’ office. She wore a T-shirt that said, "FREE AMERICA FROM ISRAEL," with the image of an Israeli flag over the mouth of the Statue of Liberty.
The back of her shirt read: "ISRAEL GETS BILLIONS / AMERICANS PAY THE BILL."
She accused Jeffries of being "a mouthpiece for Israel, AIPAC, the Israeli lobby," and declared: "The Democrats are spineless."
After the vote paving the way for Jeffries to become House speaker Wednesday, the activists in the red-green-green-blue alliance weren't relenting in their anti-Schumer campaign.

At 2:05 p.m., the Council on American-Islamic Relations issued an "Action Alert" to support Van Hollen against "AIPAC's toxic influence over our politics." The appeal followed an endorsement of Van Hollen by the U.S. Council of Muslim Organizations, an umbrella coalition of American Muslim institutions.

At 4:49 p.m., a far-left 501(c)(4) political nonprofit, Showing Up for Racial Justice, which organizes "white people for racial and economic justice," announced it is hosting phone banks to "FIRE CHUCK."

Around then, Sunrise Movement posted a video of actor Mark Ruffalo, speaking to the camera as he blasted Schumer's support of an environmental bill, gripping his forehead with his hands and saying, "God bless him," as he spoke about Schumer.
A follower responded: "Sorry folks but red and blue are two sides of the same bloody coin."

title: Republicans hold lone Alaska House seat despite losing Senate, governor races
summary: Rep. Nick Begich won re-election to Alaska's lone House seat after ranked-choice tabulation, a rare Republican bright spot in a Democratic wave.
story: ‘Fox News @ Night’ anchor Trace Gallagher reports on Democrat Mary Peltola defeating GOP nominee Dan Sullivan in the Alaska U.S. Senate race, flipping the ninth GOP-held seat.
Rep. Nick Begich, R-Alaska, won re-election to Alaska’s lone House seat Wednesday, surviving a Democratic wave that flipped both the Senate seat and the governor’s mansion.

Begich, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump, defeated independent challenger Bill Hill, a commercial fisherman and retired teacher backed by the Alaska Democratic Party, following the state’s ranked-choice voting tabulation.

Begich’s victory, called at 9:27 p.m. ET on Wednesday – more than two weeks after Election Day – stood in sharp contrast to the rest of Alaska’s top-of-the-ticket results, where voters handed Democrats major breakthroughs despite Trump winning the state by 13% in 2024.
HUNDREDS OF SUBPOENAS FLY IN DOJ’S ‘DECOY DAN’ PROBE AS DEMOCRAT PELTOLA DECLARED WINNER IN ALASKA
Rep. Nick Begich, R-Alaska, continues to show political strength in the state that has flipped Democratic in this midterm election cycle. (Nathaniel Wilder/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The race was among the final House contests called nationally after the Nov. 3 general election, offering a rare bright spot for Republicans in a midterm cycle that saw Democrats seize control of both chambers of Congress. Democrats thus far hold a 257-172 majority in the House, having flipped 46 seats to just three for Republicans. There are three races that remain too close to call.

"This process requires engagement, and the perspectives brought forward during the campaign added value for Alaskans as they made important decisions about their vote in this race," Begich said in a statement after his victory.
Hill, who campaigned on lowering costs, curbing big money in politics and pushing back against billionaires, said he called Begich to concede and congratulate him.
"I wished him well as he continues representing Alaska in Congress, because all Alaskans have a stake in his success," Hill said in a statement.
ALASKA DEM PELTOLA DEFEATS SULLIVAN, FLIPPING 9TH GOP SENATE SEAT AFTER 'DECOY DAN' UPROAR

One day before Begich’s race was called, Democrat Mary Peltola unseated second-term Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska. Peltola — who previously represented Alaska in the U.S. House before losing to Begich in 2024 — became the first Alaska native elected to the Senate and the first Democrat to win a Senate race in the state in nearly two decades. Her victory cemented a 56-44 Democratic Senate majority, the party's largest since 2009.

"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my career to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," Peltola wrote on X.

Democrats also secured the Alaska governor’s office for the first time in nearly 30 years, with Democrat Jonathan S. Kreiss-Tomkins winning the open-seat race to succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy.

Throughout the House campaign, Begich pitched himself as an effective advocate aligned with Trump’s push to expand oil, gas and resource development in Alaska. But the final stretch of the race was overshadowed by controversy surrounding Democrat Eric Hafner, a perennial candidate with no ties to Alaska who is currently serving a sentence in a federal prison in New York following a 2022 conviction for threatening to kill judges, police officers and others.
PELTOLA SAYS ALASKA ‘VOTED FOR CHANGE’ IN SENATE RACE

Hafner, whose state election booklet biography made no mention of his incarceration, captured nearly 8% of the first-round vote. In the closing weeks of the race, Hill’s campaign distributed stickers and yard signs branding Hafner a "fake ‘Democrat,’" while state party officials spent thousands of dollars on text messages to clarify that Hill was the party’s endorsed candidate after mysterious, unsourced texts circulated promoting Hafner.

Hafner’s mother, Carol "Kitty" Hafner — who also lacks ties to Alaska and finished sixth in the state's August Senate primary — dismissed claims that her son was recruited as a spoiler, writing in an email to The Associated Press that his runs have been "entirely independent of any influencers" and adding, "Tell President Trump to Pardon Eric Hafner!"
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Controversy over alleged ballot spoilers also marked the Senate race, where independent candidate Dan J. Sullivan Jr. drew suspicion due to sharing a name with the Republican incumbent. Following reports that members of Peltola’s team helped recruit Sullivan Jr. into the race, the U.S. Justice Department opened a criminal investigation and Gov. Dunleavy ordered a state inquiry. Peltola has repeatedly denied any involvement.
"I personally know that I am innocent, so I don’t spend a lot of time hand-wringing" about it, Peltola said Wednesday.
The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: China blocks Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Putin-Xi meeting over question to Trump
summary: Chinese officials barred Bloomberg's Annmarie Hordern from the meeting of President Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin after her earlier question.
story: A historic trilateral meeting takes place as President Donald Trump holds talks with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, China, to address key global issues. Fox News' Bill Melugin delivers updates from Shenzhen, while American Strategy Group president Brian Kennedy joins to analyze the geopolitical significance of these high-stakes discussions.

Chinese officials barred a Bloomberg reporter from a high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin after she asked a question during an earlier bilateral session.

The clash over press access unfolded on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, China, where the three leaders gathered for their first-ever three-way meeting to discuss nuclear arms control, trade and the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Despite a push from the White House to get her admitted, Chinese officials refused to budge on barring Bloomberg reporter Annmarie Hordern from the room.
Hordern was blocked after she called out a question to Trump during his earlier one-on-one meeting with Xi: "President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?"
CHINA'S XI SURPRISES TRUMP AT TARMAC, RECIPROCATING GESTURE SHOWN MONTHS AGO

Chinese President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin take part in a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 19, 2026. (Mandel NGAN / AFP via Getty Images)

A second reporter also started to ask a question during the bilateral session but was shushed by Chinese officials. Beijing subsequently passed along a message to the U.S. travel pool warning that yelling questions is considered "extremely rude" and that journalists would be pulled from the room if they did so.

A White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity surrounding the issue, said Chinese officials insisted Hordern not be allowed into the trilateral meeting even as the White House advocated for her inclusion.

President Donald Trump, left, speaks during a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (Andres Martinez Casares/Pool Photo via AP)
TRUMP BRINGS TWO DIVIDED CABINET HEAVYWEIGHTS TO CHINA AS CONTROVERSY HANGS OVER HIGH-STAKES TALKS

The dispute over press rules stood out alongside the friendly tone Trump sought to project toward both leaders during the summit. Trump praised his friendship with Xi, who greeted Air Force One on the tarmac Wednesday with a one-armed hug and called Putin "my friend" ahead of a separate 40-minute sit-down.
Tensions over artificial intelligence, however, still hung over the meetings.

Trump's ally Jensen Huang resigned last week as the CEO of Nvidia after confessing to an extramarital affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whose company helped give China access to Nvidia's advanced computer chips used to develop AI models. Beijing has denied that Alice Huang was a Chinese government agent.
Fox News’ Kaitlin Sprague and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Democrats could enter congressional majority in a government shutdown
summary: House Republicans on Capitol Hill worry Democrats' post-midterm clout could trigger another government shutdown ahead of the Dec. 11 funding deadline.
story: Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen floated using a government shutdown threat to end the war in Iran during an interview on Thursday.
There's nonzero chance Democrats could kick off their newfound dominance on Capitol Hill with another government shutdown.

Several House Republicans told Fox News Digital they were worried about Democrats in both chambers making unreasonable and highly partisan demands ahead of the Dec. 11, 2026, federal funding deadline, potentially paralyzing the U.S. government until a deal could be reached.
"I’m concerned," Rep. Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., told Fox News Digital. "I would say it is on my threat button, as a SEAL, it’s a five-meter target."
Rep. Mike Haridopolos, R-Fla., suggested Democrats' recent midterm victories would give them the confidence to allow a shutdown to happen.
REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS DODGED A FALL SHUTDOWN, BUT THE REAL FIGHT LOOMS

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., sued President Donald Trump and his administration for the president's mail-in balloting executive order. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

"I’m very worried about it. Unfortunately, the Democrat tactics of shutting down the government worked for them politically, so I’m afraid they’re going to go back to their winning playbook," he said.
SCHUMER, JEFFRIES SIDESTEP QUESTIONS ON NUKING FILIBUSTER, LAUNCHING ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER BLUE WAVE

Congress opted to delay the government funding fight until after the midterm elections, passing a simple extension of fiscal year (FY) 2026 spending levels called a continuing resolution (CR) from the beginning of FY 2027 on Oct. 1 through Dec. 11.
Republicans who spoke with Fox News Digital expressed varying levels of optimism about whether they could hash out a budget for FY 2027 before the end of the year.
SENATE REPUBLICANS PLAN 54-DAY BLITZ TO PUSH TRUMP'S AGENDA BEFORE DEMOCRATS SEIZE POWER
"What we should get done is move every appropriation's bill we can," said Rep. Mark Messmer, R-Ind.
Asked about whether he's concerned about a shutdown, he said, "That's up to the Democrats in the Senate."
Most people who spoke with Fox News Digital said they believe another CR extending early into 2028 is the most likely path, which would give Democrats more control over writing it.
Rep. Mike Haridopolos leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on June 10, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
But for Democrats, unsurprisingly, Republicans are to blame.
CHRIS VAN HOLLEN FLOATS USING GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN THREAT TO FORCE TRUMP TO END IRAN WAR

"I wanted to finish the bills by the end of the year. We had the opportunity to do that, and the Republican side of the Senate has held out," Rep. Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, said.
DeLauro said last week she wanted to see a short-term CR extending only as far as March.
MAJORITY LEADER THUNE SAYS SENATE GOP WON'T 'STAND IDLY BY' AS DEMOCRATS TAKE CONTROL OF CONGRESS

She suggested, however, that the Iran war could be a sticking point for Democrats down the line, telling reporters, "I can just say that we're not going to be doing billions of dollars for a war of choice."
Senate Democrats are pushing for guardrails on funding for the Iran war, and Republicans are already worried that they’ll shutter the government if they don’t get what they want.

"That is playing with fire for sure," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., told Fox News Digital. "It's one thing to pound your chest and talk about it. It's another thing to put America's military men and women in jeopardy."

U.S. House Appropriations Committee ranking member Rosa DeLauro talks to reporters following a House Democratic caucus meeting at the Capitol Sept. 29, 2025, in Washington. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

A trio of Senate Democrats, Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., and Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., are pushing an amendment to a forthcoming bill that would stymie funds from helping the war effort, something that Republicans largely won’t support.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who is running to topple Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., as Democratic leader, is supportive of the effort.
"For starters, we need a clear amendment that says we can't spend money on offensive operations because we do need to end the war, but we also need to bring down costs now," Van Hollen said.
