title: Senate passes bill simplifying permitting rules to build in America, sending it to House
summary: The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday night to pass a sweeping bill to simplify and overhaul permitting rules for energy and infrastructure projects.
story: WASHINGTON — The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday night to pass a sweeping bill to simplify and overhaul permitting rules for energy and infrastructure projects.

The bill, called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, was crafted by an unusual coalition of Sens. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va.; Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I.; Mike Lee, R-Utah; and Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.

The legislation would revise and speed up environmental reviews with tighter deadlines; accelerate electricity transmission; restrict the power of federal agencies to revoke existing permits; and reduce chokepoints for approving and completing projects.
To conservatives, it’s about cutting government bureaucracy.

“For far too long, critical investments in our nation’s infrastructure, energy production, and economy have been forced to sit on the sidelines due to endless red tape, duplicative reviews, and regulatory uncertainty,” Capito said.
For liberals, it’s an opportunity to make it easier to build long-sought projects, including clean energy, and address high costs.
“Democrats are focused on lowering energy costs, reducing emissions, and stopping data centers’ free ride,” Whitehouse said. “Americans will start to get some relief quickly if this bill passes.”

In an attempt to alleviate Americans’ concerns about data centers, the bill would require “new data centers of 20 megawatts or more to pay the full incremental cost of the infrastructure built to serve them,” according to the Bipartisan Policy Center.

The legislation sparked opposition from some environmental groups and Native American tribal organizations, which objected to easing reviews and consultation rules that can be used to protect their interests. The bulk of the opposition in the Senate came from Democrats.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Still, the willingness to simplify permitting rules represents a philosophical shift for the Democrats who endorsed it. Part of the reason is that liberal policy experts recognized that existing laws hinder their own goals.

“This removes a lot of the obstacles that hamstrung [Joe] Biden’s climate investments,” said Adam Jentleson, a former Senate Democratic aide and founder of the research group Searchlight Institute. “A big part of the Inflation Reduction Act — a lot of the projects couldn’t break ground because of all the red tape.”
The bill still needs approval from the House, where Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., expressed optimism that Congress will send a bill to President Donald Trump’s desk.

“Well, we want to see a bill pass both chambers,” Scalise said when asked if the House will take up the Senate version of the legislation. “Obviously, the details matter. ... Hopefully, they pass a good bill back, and if not, we’ll work out those differences. But we want to get a bill to the president’s desk, and that’s still got a great chance to happen.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said the clearest path to making a law is for the House to take the Senate’s measure and pass it, noting that it has been through extensive debate.

“It has been litigated now for months. Continues to be,” Thune told reporters. “Everything gets more complicated over here procedurally, and if it were to go over there and then come back over here, I can’t predict what happens. So hopefully there’ll be the critical mass there to move it. ... It’s been through the full monty when it comes to the legislating process.”

title: Justice Department seeks dismissal of its lawsuit in Alaska Senate race
summary: The Trump administration had sought to block certification of the election results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan lost. Democrat Mary Peltola won the race.

Democratic candidate Mary Peltola ended up winning the race this week.

The lawsuit, filed by the Justice Department in October, followed President Donald Trump’s repeated claims that the inclusion of candidate Dan J. Sullivan on the ballot, alongside Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, was a stunt to “defraud” voters.
In its filing Thursday, the Justice Department asked the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to declare the lawsuit moot, citing Peltola’s victory.

“The United States brought this lawsuit to ensure that the State and its officers fulfill Alaska’s obligation to protect the integrity of its election,” Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward wrote in the filing.
He added that the government “therefore reluctantly acknowledges that there no longer exists any means” of examining whether votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan were intended to be cast for the incumbent.

title: White House national cyber director is leaving the administration after series of tech outages
summary: Sean Cairncross has played a key role in crafting AI policy for the Trump administration. His immediate replacement is Kirsten A. Davies.
story: White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving the Trump administration, a White House official confirmed Thursday, in the wake of tech outages that hit both the private and public sectors.
Cairncross will be replaced by Kirsten A. Davies, who currently serves as the chief information officer at the Defense Department, a source close to the White House told NBC News.
Davies will serve in an acting capacity, the source said. The position requires Senate confirmation.
Axios was first to report the personnel changes.
Cairncross has served as head of the Office of the National Cyber Director since August 2025. The office oversees all government cybersecurity policy and strategy.

He has been directly involved with the White House’s deliberations over AI policy, including after Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick directed Anthropic to take down its two most powerful AI systems over the summer due to national security concerns.

Cairncross is leaving his post after a series of tech outages affected both private companies and government agencies over the past week. Administration officials as well as Democratic members of Congress have said the outages do not appear to be the result of cyberattacks, though some have suggested AI may have played a role.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The White House, when reached for comment Thursday night, did not provide details about the staffing changes.
Cairncross’ previous White House roles include senior adviser to the White House chief of staff during Trump’s first term.

During the 2016 election cycle, he was the Republican National Committee’s chief operating officer. He worked for the RNC again during the 2024 cycle, serving as then-chief operating officer Chris LaCivita’s deputy.
Davies posted on X about her new position.

“Our nation stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected. Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come …but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future,” she wrote. “Under President Trump’s leadership we will have a more secure, resilient; and supercharged technological future.”

The source close to the White House said Davies will strengthen the president’s cybersecurity team, which includes Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who also serves as national security adviser.

title: Walmart stocks up on inflation-weary shoppers ahead of the holidays
summary: Walmart raised its sales outlook and reported gaining market share as it lures more affluent shoppers who are hunting for deals amid high inflation.
story: Walmart isn’t just adding inventory for the holiday shopping season; it’s also racking up more customers looking for discounts as inflation maintains its grip on the U.S. economy.

The retail giant on Thursday said it gained market share and raised its sales outlook for the third time this year as bargain hunters across income levels hit stores and fill their online shopping carts.
“Looking ahead, we expect a strong holiday season,” CEO John Furner said on an earnings call with analysts Thursday.

Walmart, which is generally considered a barometer for the U.S. economy, has long been a go-to store for consumers seeking discounts. Rising prices have pushed many consumers to rethink where they shop, and Walmart has benefited from more higher-income shoppers. As it draws more affluent customers, the company has launched a fashion-forward women’s apparel brand and expanded its e-commerce and advertising businesses.

Walmart isn’t alone in gaining momentum with thrifty shoppers ahead of the holidays. Rivals Target and Costco are also seeing customers respond to their value offerings, both posting sales increases and Target raising its outlook.
The results illustrate the resilience of American consumers, who keep spending even while grocery and gas prices rise and paycheck growth lags the pace of inflation.
“In spite of that, consumers are finding ways to get what they need for their families,” Matthew Shay, president of the National Retail Federation, told NBC News on Wednesday.

Still, it’s shaping up to be a strong holiday season, and not just for Walmart. The National Retail Federation forecasts that sales in November and December will top $1 trillion in the U.S. for the first time. But that doesn’t necessarily mean consumers are buying more items; rather, they’re paying a higher price at checkout.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

This season, Walmart said it lowered the price of 7,700 items by the end of the third quarter while expanding deals on groceries. The company said it will also offer a Thanksgiving meal basket for 10 at $3.50 per person, including turkey, Stove Top stuffing, mashed potatoes and other staples.

Walmart also raked in more revenue from its membership fees, which surged 17% in the quarter. The company announced a bundled deal that includes memberships to Walmart+ and its warehouse-club subsidiary Sam’s Club, as well as perks including free access to streaming platforms and gas savings.

While shoppers seem to be sold on Walmart heading into the holidays, Wall Street was a bit more cautious. The company’s stock slipped about 1% to $126 a share amid a broader market sell-off Thursday, even as quarterly revenue and profit surpassed investors’ expectations.
Goldman Sachs analysts said they still rated Walmart’s stock a “buy,” projecting it’ll hit $132 a share.
Nonetheless, they also flagged risks to the company’s outlook, including the potential for an economic slowdown and more intense price competition from its big-box and online rivals.

title: El Niño strikes again, breaking rain records in San Francisco and along Florida’s Atlantic coast
summary: A strong El Nino is once again rearing its head, with storms breaking rainfall records and causing coastal flooding in both California and Florida.
story: As storms pound both coasts on Wednesday and Thursday, a strong El Niño is once again rearing its head, breaking rainfall records and causing coastal flooding in California and Florida.
Downtown San Francisco set a new record for daily rainfall Wednesday, at 2.64 inches. The previous record was 2.24 inches on Nov. 18, 1918.

“Yesterday completely smashed those records,” said Anamaria Navarette, a National Weather Service meteorologist in the agency’s San Francisco Bay Area office. “El Niño certainly is playing a part in the event.”

Two waterspouts — a rotating, tornado-like column of moisture over the sea — formed in the San Francisco Bay on Wednesday, and another near Santa Cruz, to the south. Gusty winds downed trees and power lines, while rain soaked burn scars from past wildfires, prompting flash flood warnings.

title: Trump’s symbolic summit: From the Politics Desk
summary: In today’s edition, Andrea Mitchell dives into the fallout from President Donald Trump’s trilateral meeting in China.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, Andrea Mitchell dives into the fallout from President Donald Trump’s trilateral meeting in China. Plus, Sarah Sternhagen explains why Republicans weren’t far off from suffering even deeper midterm losses.
— Adam Wollner
Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi was light on results, but heavy on symbolism

It was an image the White House heralded as historic: an American president holding a summit with the leaders of China and Russia, the three commanders of the world’s largest nuclear arsenals. To some, it had echoes of Yalta in 1945, when Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill, and Joseph Stalin divided Europe, with post-war consequences lasting nearly a half-century.

This time, substantively, there were no concrete results. But it did send a signal across the globe to see President Donald Trump, the leader of the world’s foremost democracy, standing shoulder to shoulder with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin without even paying lip service to human rights, press freedoms or political prisoners. Afterward, China and Russia issued statements that didn’t dispute the absence of agreements. There was no progress on nuclear proliferation, trade or critical minerals.

Trump’s warm embrace with Xi in Shenzhen can be justified by the importance of maintaining a constructive dialogue between the world’s two most powerful economies. Much harder to justify in the eyes of NATO allies is Trump’s affectionate greeting for Putin, calling the invader of Ukraine, “my friend.” Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk posted on X, “God protect us from such friends.”

Perhaps appearing side by side with the two strongmen — both, in effect, leaders for life — was designed to bolster a U.S. president politically weakened by a tsunami-sized midterm defeat, and frustrated by two wars he promised to end quickly. In the case of Ukraine, Trump pledged during the 2024 campaign he could solve the war in one day after taking office. After joining Israel last February in attacking Iran, Trump said the conflict would be over in several weeks.

After leaving China, Trump joined a call with his two envoys, Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner, who were in Berlin to meet with Ukrainian officials and an eight-member European negotiating team working on security guarantees and an economic reconstruction plan for Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC News’ Richard Engel of Trump meeting with Putin and Xi without him, “You can’t decide about some country, even a small country, without this country.”

Addressing his nation today, Zelenskyy said the U.S. representatives were going “to provide the necessary information about the U.S. president’s negotiations” and that “we and the Europeans share a clear common position: matters concerning Ukraine must be decided with Ukraine’s participation, and matters concerning Europe must be decided with Europe’s participation.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

But prior to the China meeting, European leaders had been assured that Trump, Putin and Xi would not deal with Ukraine without Europe. Punctuating the challenge, Russia attacked Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities during the Shenzhen summit and the hours after. Ukraine drove home its resistance by attacking a key bridge linking Russia with Crimea, a project heavy with strategic and symbolic importance to Putin.

Trump recently repeated his belief that Zelenskyy could have prevented the war — apparently ignoring that Putin invaded a sovereign state in violation of past nonaggression pacts. And U.S. negotiators have been pressuring Ukraine for concessions, although Putin has given no indication he is ready to compromise. The Shenzhen summit will likely reinforce the Russian leader’s confidence that he can count on support from Trump.
How the blue wave could have been even bigger
The 2026 elections were already devastating for Republicans, with the party losing a net of at least 42 House seats.

But it was close to being much worse for the party. Among the House Republican candidates who managed to win, 26 of them did so by less than 3 points. It’s a number that’s much higher compared to recent midterms, as the chart below illustrates. For instance, in 2018 — another blue wave year — half as many (13) GOP House candidates won their races by less than 3 points.

Put another way, only 41 House Republicans won at least 60% of the vote this year. By comparison, more than four times as many (174) House Democrats surpassed that threshold. In the 2022 midterms, when President Joe Biden’s low approval rating weighed down his party, 126 Democratic House candidates still managed to take at least 60% of the vote, while 153 Republicans did.

title: Trump gives posthumous pardon to baseball’s Pete Rose, who pleaded guilty to tax evasion
summary: The baseball great, who died in 2024, pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been banned from the sport for betting on games.
story: President Donald Trump announced on social media Thursday that he has pardoned the late Pete Rose, baseball’s all-time hits leader.

“I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND, whose record of 4,256 Hits in a Season will never be broken,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social as he was returning from a meeting in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Rose had 4,256 hits in his major league career, not in a single season. Trump’s post was later edited to correct that achievement.
Trump added that Rose “was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame.”

Rose died in 2024 at age 83. He pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been permanently banned from baseball after he gambled on his own team as a player and manager. That ban was posthumously lifted last year after repeated requests from Trump.
MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said at the time that permanent ineligibility “ends upon the passing of the disciplined individual.”
Trump, who’d advocated for Rose’s inclusion in the Baseball Hall of Fame for years, announced his plans to pardon Rose in March 2025.
“He never betted against himself, or the other team. He had the most hits, by far, in baseball history, and won more games than anyone in sports history,” Trump said then.
Rose denied he’d gambled on baseball for almost 15 years before admitting in his 2004 autobiography that he’d bet both as a player and a manager, but never against his own team.
Rose played 24 seasons in Major League Baseball, the last three as a player-manager for the Cincinnati Reds, where he played for the bulk of his career.
The National Baseball Hall of Fame has said that Rose’s removal from the ineligible list means his candidacy can be considered when its Classic Baseball Era Committee meets in December of next year.

title: Talking Shop with comedian Heather McMahan
summary: Comedian Heather McMahan is going on tour in 2027. She’s not traveling without her favorite packing cubes, snacks, lashes and compression socks.
story: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys.

One of the things Heather McMahan has become an expert in throughout her career as a comedian is traveling. I know that might not totally make sense at first, but when you look at her 2027 schedule alone, you get it. Her Burning Down the House Tour is taking her across the country starting in January,  she’s hosting her Absolutely Knot Cruise in May from Miami to the Bahamas, and somehow between all of that, she’s also recording her podcast and making it back home to Atlanta as much as possible. McMahan has packing, flying and on-the-go glam down to a science, and turning a hotel room into a home is her specialty.

Because she’s such a travel professional, McMahan recently partnered with Hilton to debut its New Ways to Stay campaign, which included a pop-up experience in New York City’s Time Square and a vacation sweepstakes that sent six people on surprise solo getaways. I got to talk to McMahan at the pop-up, who told me that while there’s numerous luxury amenities at Hilton locations worldwide, there’s one she looks forward to the most.

“I know you’re expecting me to say a nice gym,” she joked, “but I actually love that perfect 5 p.m. happy hour moment where you’re sitting in a great cocktail bar in a gorgeous hotel and you’re having your aperol spritz or whatever your drink of choice is — even if it’s a Diet Coke with a lime in it. You’re sitting there and you’re like, ‘We’re here. We arrived. Look at all the things we’ve done in this brand-new city or destination that we’ve been in today.’”
McMahan also gave me a rundown of her travel essentials, including the top four things she brings for her dressing room while she’s on tour.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Weezie Packing Cube Bundle (3 pieces)

“When I’m packing, I have every intention of keeping things organized. It’s all in the cubes, and then my husband calls me Hurricane Heather because when I get to a hotel, everything explodes out of my bag,” says McMahan. “He’s like, ‘Heather, this is the most organized chaos.’ But I know where my stuff is. It’s in the bags, that are in the other bags, that are in the cubes, that are shoved somewhere. Just don’t touch it.”

If there’s one thing McMahan will admit to over-packing, it’s underwear. “Listen, I’m going to tell you right now: pack more underwear than you think, alright? Just grab a handful and at least throw an extra 10 in there because you never know,” she says. “But whatever you forgot at home, Hilton’s got it, so call down to the front desk, and be like, “Hi, I need a toothbrush kit.” Come on — they’re thinking three steps ahead. You think this is their first rodeo? They know what’s going on.”
Spanx AirEssentials Half Zip

“I like to look nice on an airplane, so I’m always going to have a nice jacket, a blazer or a cashmere sweater,” says McMahan. “It’s freezing on airplanes, so it’s a way to kind of pull yourself together. You can have sweats on underneath, but just have a nice blazer or cashmere sweater.” One of her favorite sweaters to throw on is Spanx’s AirEssentials Half Zip, which is made from lightweight, silky-soft fabric to keep her cozy.
All in Motion Women’s Essential Compression Socks

McMahan also always wears compression socks to help with circulation on an airplane, especially because she often flies multiple times a week. She loves All in Motion’s Women’s Essential Compression Socks from Target, which comes in a two pack. They’re lightly cushioned, extend up to the knees and have a wide cuff, making them easy to put on and take off. There’s built-in arch support, too.
We can help you find
Barebells Salty Peanut Protein Bars

“I’m one of those people who has every intention to download a movie or a new show on my iPad before I get on a flight, but I am just scrolling on TikTok for seven and a half hours while I fly to Istanbul. That’s just what I do,” says McMahan. She’s low maintenance about her in-flight entertainment, but she doesn’t mess around when it comes to snacks.

“You do not want to see me panicking if you think my blood sugar has gotten low, so I’ve always got some sort of sweet treat and a protein snack,” says McMahan. Her two go-tos are Unreal’s Dark Chocolate Coconut Bars and Barebells’ Salty Peanut Protein Bars. But she has a savory favorite that she also can’t live without: “If you travel around with a hunk of parmigiano reggio cheese, you’re good to go,” says McMahan. “Just a little health tip: have a hunk of cheese in your back pocket.”
Spindrift Sparkling Water

“I’m pretty easy backstage,” says McMahan when I asked her about her pre-show routine. “I need quiet time before a show. I like to decompress before I turn it on, so I listen to a very specific Spotify playlist called ‘Cocktail Jazz.’ Then I do a full glam beat, and then I eat a hunk of cheese and a handful of salami, and chug a Spindrift — that’s what I do before a show. It’s really not that exciting or glamorous. It’s just a little salami, a little cheese and a glam beat. That’s all you need.”
Ardell Naked Lashes 421

Speaking of her glam, McMahan says the number one most important part of it is her lashes, whether she’s going on stage or running errands at home. “I am wildly dedicated to Ardell Lashes,” she says. “I can put these on literally with my eyes closed or on the back of a jet ski. I wear Ardell’s 420s, 421s and 424s. I don’t leave the house without a lash.”
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who leads our Talking Shop series, interviewing people like Paris Hilton, Maureen Kelly, Lindsay Hubbard and Chase Crawford. To write this article, I talked to comedian Heather McMahan about her favorite travel essentials, especially when she’s on tour, and her partnership with Hilton.

title: How to find worthwhile deals during Black Friday and Cyber Monday: a step-by-step, expert-approved guide
summary: Are Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals actually worth it? Shopping experts share tips on what to buy, what to skip and how to find genuine discounts.
story: Retailers started rolling out their early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals this week, so I’m sure you’ve asked yourself: are these discounts actually worth it? I’ve covered the massive sales for over six years, and I can say with certainty that they offer some of the year’s lowest prices across categories. But it takes a little bit of work to find the absolute best deals, and you have to strategize beforehand to save the most money.

To help you make a Black Friday and Cyber Monday game plan, I put together this guide filled with tips and tricks I swear by. I also talked to experts to get their advice about what to buy, what to skip, how to find the top deals and whether shopping in-person versus online makes a difference anymore.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
What are the best things to buy during Black Friday and Cyber Monday?

If you have electronics on your wish list — or are buying a gift for someone who does — now is your time to buy. Tech sees some of the strongest discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, especially when it comes to devices like TVs, headphones and video game consoles, says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, a shopping and savings strategist at Rakuten, an online and in-store cashback platform. As a baseline, Vipin Porwal, the founder and consumer savings expert at Smarty, an online shopping rewards app, expects at least 30 percent off in most cases, except for TVs and computers, which are usually in the 20 to 25 percent off range.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday video game bundles are particularly lucrative. It’s one of the only times a year I see brands like Nintendo, Xbox and PlayStation sell their most popular console, game and digital subscription for less than each item would cost if you bought them individually.

Toys is one of the most competitive categories during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, both in terms of discounts and demand. You usually get at least 30 percent off, says Porwal, and the most popular toys sell out quickly — I’m talking a couple of hours, maximum. Once you see prices drop, buy your must-haves immediately. Some of the hottest toys and collectibles to watch this season are the Beyblade X, Jellycats, KPop Demon Hunters toys, Lego Pokémon and SMART Play, NeeDohs, Pokémon Pikachu Puppetronic, Sesame Street Tickle Me Elmo Giggle Max and Toy Story 5 toys, according to Adobe.

Clothes and shoes typically get marked down by at least 20 to 25 percent during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, says Porwal. Many brands run sitewide sales, so their entire inventory is marked down, while department stores and big-box retailers put most of their stock on clearance to get rid of it before the new year.

Almost every small home and kitchen appliance you can think of gets discounted during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, including that Vitamix blender or Dyson vacuum you’re dreaming about. In addition to items you use year-round, keep an eye on seasonal appliances, like space heaters and snow blowers, as well as tableware, home decor and other essentials you’ll need to host guests during the holidays, says Gerstley.

Don’t forget to think beyond tangible products during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, says Mackenzie Shand, executive editor at RetailMeNot, a digital coupon, promo code and cashback platform. There are lots of deals on subscriptions, experiences and activities, too. “Many streaming services host Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, which can lower the cost of your entertainment bill for the entire year,” she says. “Meanwhile, if you have travel plans coming up, be on the lookout for deals on things like passes to zoos, aquariums and other recreation-type places in your area.” Fitness classes, gym memberships, beauty appointments, educational platforms and event tickets also often drop in price.

Additionally, while Travel Tuesday, on December 1 this year, is a dedicated day for travel deals, you’ll start seeing offers well before then. Hotels, resorts, tour groups, rental home and car booking companies, cruise lines and flight booking platforms are starting to roll out their sales now, making it the ideal time to plan a trip. You’ll see travel essentials on sale, too, like suitcases, toiletry bags and packing cubes.

Because retailers know Black Friday and Cyber Monday are prime times for holiday shopping, many discount gift cards for literally everything: stores across categories, restaurants, movie theatres, spas, streaming services, food delivery platforms, and more. “As long as you plan to gift or use this gift card, you are basically getting free money from these deals,” says Shand. There are also strong discounts on gift sets, like those that bundle beauty products, gourmet food and beverages, travel essentials and accessories. You buy these sets, wrap them and give them to your recipient rather than having to curate a selection yourself.

What products should you avoid buying during Black Friday and Cyber Monday?

No category is totally off limits during Black Friday and Cyber Monday — if you do the work, you can find a worthwhile deal on almost anything since the majority of retailers participate in the biggest shopping events of the year. But if you’re trying to narrow down your list, here’s what experts recommend waiting on and when to buy it instead:

Winter clothes and shoes: wait until end-of-season clearance sales in January and FebruaryMattresses, furniture and major home and kitchen appliances: wait until three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ DayBed and bath linens, like sheets and towels: wait until “white sales” in January and three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ DayFitness equipment: wait until New Year’s sales in JanuaryHoliday decor: wait until after the holiday season to refresh your collection and save it for next year
Winter clothes and shoes: wait until end-of-season clearance sales in January and February
Mattresses, furniture and major home and kitchen appliances: wait until three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ Day
Bed and bath linens, like sheets and towels: wait until “white sales” in January and three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ Day
Fitness equipment: wait until New Year’s sales in January
Holiday decor: wait until after the holiday season to refresh your collection and save it for next year
Are Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals worse than last year?

No, Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals aren’t worse than last year, but they’re not dramatically better either, says Claudia Townsend, a consumer behavior researcher and expert and marketing professor at the University of Miami. “Prices have risen, while discount percentages are likely to remain roughly the same as last year,” she says. “This means that a 25 percent discount, for example, will yield a higher final price if the item’s starting price is higher than it was a year ago.”

That said, Black Friday and Cyber Monday are still the biggest, highest-revenue days for retail of the year. Retailers want to draw customers in with deals, so most save their lowest prices for late November. But a discount isn’t a compelling enough reason alone for shoppers to spend anymore, says Shand — they’re being much more thoughtful about scoping out real deals to get the best overall value, not just the lowest price.
How do you find the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals?

“The most common mistake is allowing in-the-moment sales and marketing cues define one’s shopping list,” says Townsend. “That’s how people end up “saving” 40 percent on items they never intended to buy. I recommend that consumers create a list with a budget and a target price for each item, and commit to purchasing only when a deal reaches that price.”

Some retailers let you make shopping lists in their apps or on their websites and, along with certain cashback extensions, let you set up notifications when items’ prices drop so you can start evaluating immediately. That means you don’t have to do any browsing that might lead to impulse purchases — you stay zeroed in on your list the entire time.

Free tools like CamelCamelCamel, Keepa and Honey show you a product’s price history, as do built-in features on some retailers’ websites. Use them to determine whether an item dropped in price from a steady baseline, making it a legitimate deal, or if it’s marked down from an inflated baseline.

Be sure to also use price-tracking tools to figure out what a specific product cost during Black Friday and Cyber Monday last year. That serves as a great comparison point, especially for early deals: If a product’s price dropped more during last year’s Black Friday to Cyber Monday period than the two weeks before it, you can expect a brand to follow the same pattern this year, giving you an idea about when you should finally add to cart and check out.
Overall, “if the deal price matches or beats the item’s lowest price over the past year, it’s likely a good deal,” says Townsend.

Before checking out, compare the price of a specific product across multiple retailers to make sure you’re getting the absolute lowest offer, says Shand. Look beyond the actual discount, too. Factor in shipping fees, extra perks like free installation and where you get the most cash back, for example.

The discount itself is your starting point. Can you bring down the price even more by signing up for email or SMS lists and getting an extra promo code; using a cashback extension; becoming a free loyalty member and earning rewards as you shop; or paying with a credit card that lets you earn points or cash back?

If there’s a product at the top of your or your loved one’s wish list, get it as soon as it goes on sale, so long as the retailer you’re shopping at has a price-matching policy. “If a retailer will refund the difference should the price drop more, there’s little downside to buying,” says Townsend.

Retailers stretch Black Friday and Cyber Monday out across the entire month of November, so there’s no reason to wait to buy a product if you do everything you can to make sure it’s a good deal now. In fact, because so many customers are vying for the same products, and retailers limit quantities of certain products, shopping early might be the only way to get an item in the exact color, size and style you want. “Sometimes, finding the product you actually want in stock is the deal,” says Shand. “A great deal doesn’t do you much good if the product is gone.”
Frequently asked questions
Black Friday is on November 27, 2026.
Cyber Monday is on November 30, 2026.
Black Friday and Cyber Monday start on November 27 and 30, respectively, but deals have already begun. Retailers will continue rolling out sales leading up to the actual events next week.

The best deals typically end on Cyber Monday: this year, that’s November 30, 2026. However, some sales extend into early December because retailers know people continue shopping for holiday gifts. Extended deals are usually weaker and less plentiful, though, so you’re not maximizing your budget or choosing from the best options at that point.

There’s not much of a difference between Black Friday and Cyber Monday anymore. Black Friday used to be dedicated to in-store shopping and Cyber Monday was reserved for online shopping, but now, retailers run promotions throughout all of November, not just on a specific day or two, says Gerstley. In recent years, the National Retail Federation has also found that more people shop online during Black Friday than in person, so the rulebook has totally gone out the window.

Deals are almost exactly the same on Black Friday and Cyber Monday, experts told me. On each shopping holiday, retailers add a few limited-time discounts to give shoppers new options to sift through, but overall, Cyber Monday is your last chance to shop and buy anything left on your list.
Deals are comparable in-store and online during Black Friday. Consider these factors when deciding how to shop.

Online shopping is more convenient than in-store shopping, and it’s easier to compare prices across sites, activate cashback offers and find additional promo codes, says Gerstley. That said, you can earn cash back from certain programs while shopping in person. You just have to link the card you pay with in-store to your account in the app or online. Retailers offer a wider variety of discounts online — they only have so much space on shelves in stores.Retailers want to make in-store shopping a special experience for customers on Black Friday, so they may offer exclusive deals and gifts with purchase at their locations.In-store shopping lets you try on and touch items, and take them home that day.You’ll likely have to pay shipping fees if you shop online, but you can avoid them by shopping in person. title: Larry Poindexter, ‘Days of Our Lives’ and ‘S.W.A.T.’ actor, dies after being hit by car
summary: Veteran actor Larry Poindexter — who appeared in soap operas “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital” and the movie “S.W.A.T.”
story: Veteran actor Larry Poindexter — who appeared in soap operas “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital” and the movie “S.W.A.T.” — died Wednesday, days after he was hit by a car while crossing the street near his Los Angeles home, officials said Thursday.
He was 66.

Poindexter was walking near the corner of Moorpark Street and Lankershim Boulevard on Friday, about three blocks from the actor’s home, when he was struck by a car at around 6 p.m. PT, his agent and police said.
The investigation is ongoing, an LAPD spokesperson said.
“He was picking up some dinner,” the actor’s agent, Harry Gold, told NBC News on Thursday.
Poindexter suffered broken ribs but his injuries were not believed to be fatal, according to Gold.
“They did not diagnose this as anything serious,” Gold said. “They put him in the hospital for observation and to repair some broken bones and then he passed away.”
Gold praised his client’s work ethic and diverse skill set.
“He had great musical talent, was in rock band and produced musicals,” Gold said. “That was important to him.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Poindexter’s long career includes 30 episodes on “Days of Our Lives” between 1984 and 2018 and a dozen appearances on “General Hospital” in 2005.
He played by-the-book LAPD Capt. Tom Fuller in the 2003 movie “S.W.A.T.,” supervising Samuel L. Jackson’s Sgt. Dan “Hondo” Harrelson.

“He offered wisdom I wasn’t always ready to hear, and it took me a few years to realize just how right he was about so many things,” Iacono wrote. “He taught me that being a good person and collaborator mattered just as much as being a great actor.”

Iacono posted a picture of himself flanked by his on-screen parents, Poindexter and Beth Littleford, adding that: “I’m forever honored to have played his son, and I’ll always cherish him as my second father.”
Poindexter is survived by his wife, casting director Carol Kritzer, and their twin boys, Rees and Jake.

title: Senate passes bill simplifying permitting rules to build in America, sending it to House
summary: The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday night to pass a sweeping bill to simplify and overhaul permitting rules for energy and infrastructure projects.
story: WASHINGTON — The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday night to pass a sweeping bill to simplify and overhaul permitting rules for energy and infrastructure projects.

The bill, called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, was crafted by an unusual coalition of Sens. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va.; Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I.; Mike Lee, R-Utah; and Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.

The legislation would revise and speed up environmental reviews with tighter deadlines; accelerate electricity transmission; restrict the power of federal agencies to revoke existing permits; and reduce chokepoints for approving and completing projects.
To conservatives, it’s about cutting government bureaucracy.

“For far too long, critical investments in our nation’s infrastructure, energy production, and economy have been forced to sit on the sidelines due to endless red tape, duplicative reviews, and regulatory uncertainty,” Capito said.
For liberals, it’s an opportunity to make it easier to build long-sought projects, including clean energy, and address high costs.
“Democrats are focused on lowering energy costs, reducing emissions, and stopping data centers’ free ride,” Whitehouse said. “Americans will start to get some relief quickly if this bill passes.”

In an attempt to alleviate Americans’ concerns about data centers, the bill would require “new data centers of 20 megawatts or more to pay the full incremental cost of the infrastructure built to serve them,” according to the Bipartisan Policy Center.

The legislation sparked opposition from some environmental groups and Native American tribal organizations, which objected to easing reviews and consultation rules that can be used to protect their interests. The bulk of the opposition in the Senate came from Democrats.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Still, the willingness to simplify permitting rules represents a philosophical shift for the Democrats who endorsed it. Part of the reason is that liberal policy experts recognized that existing laws hinder their own goals.

“This removes a lot of the obstacles that hamstrung [Joe] Biden’s climate investments,” said Adam Jentleson, a former Senate Democratic aide and founder of the research group Searchlight Institute. “A big part of the Inflation Reduction Act — a lot of the projects couldn’t break ground because of all the red tape.”
The bill still needs approval from the House, where Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., expressed optimism that Congress will send a bill to President Donald Trump’s desk.

“Well, we want to see a bill pass both chambers,” Scalise said when asked if the House will take up the Senate version of the legislation. “Obviously, the details matter. ... Hopefully, they pass a good bill back, and if not, we’ll work out those differences. But we want to get a bill to the president’s desk, and that’s still got a great chance to happen.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said the clearest path to making a law is for the House to take the Senate’s measure and pass it, noting that it has been through extensive debate.

“It has been litigated now for months. Continues to be,” Thune told reporters. “Everything gets more complicated over here procedurally, and if it were to go over there and then come back over here, I can’t predict what happens. So hopefully there’ll be the critical mass there to move it. ... It’s been through the full monty when it comes to the legislating process.”

title: Trump gives posthumous pardon to baseball’s Pete Rose, who pleaded guilty to tax evasion
summary: The baseball great, who died in 2024, pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been banned from the sport for betting on games.
story: President Donald Trump announced on social media Thursday that he has pardoned the late Pete Rose, baseball’s all-time hits leader.

“I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND, whose record of 4,256 Hits in a Season will never be broken,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social as he was returning from a meeting in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Rose had 4,256 hits in his major league career, not in a single season. Trump’s post was later edited to correct that achievement.
Trump added that Rose “was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame.”

Rose died in 2024 at age 83. He pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been permanently banned from baseball after he gambled on his own team as a player and manager. That ban was posthumously lifted last year after repeated requests from Trump.
MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said at the time that permanent ineligibility “ends upon the passing of the disciplined individual.”
Trump, who’d advocated for Rose’s inclusion in the Baseball Hall of Fame for years, announced his plans to pardon Rose in March 2025.
“He never betted against himself, or the other team. He had the most hits, by far, in baseball history, and won more games than anyone in sports history,” Trump said then.
Rose denied he’d gambled on baseball for almost 15 years before admitting in his 2004 autobiography that he’d bet both as a player and a manager, but never against his own team.
Rose played 24 seasons in Major League Baseball, the last three as a player-manager for the Cincinnati Reds, where he played for the bulk of his career.
The National Baseball Hall of Fame has said that Rose’s removal from the ineligible list means his candidacy can be considered when its Classic Baseball Era Committee meets in December of next year.

title: How a rocket scientist is fueling the NFL’s best defense
summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ defense is the top-rated unit in the entire NFL — and a former rocket scientist may be the reason why.
story: The Minnesota Vikings’ defense is the type of unit that unleashes pure terror on its opponents, a whirring buzz saw of blitzes coming from all levels of the field and entirely unpredictable.

It leads the NFL in total touchdowns allowed (just 12 scores this season), average points allowed per game (14) and total number of sacks (37) — a testament to making life quite miserable for opposing quarterbacks.

But one of the untold secrets of their success might be that acclaimed defensive coordinator Brian Flores happily accepts input from all corners, and that includes rocket scientists. In this case, it’s the team’s assistant defensive backs coach, Chenzo Funari, who until a few years ago was working on SpaceX’s combustion devices group and the company’s Starship system.
The 32-year-old said he questioned whether the role was “bringing me kind of the fulfillment in life that I thought it would.”

title: Troy Aikman escalates feud with Joe Buck, says broadcast partner ‘always wanted a one-man booth’
summary: This NFL season was supposed to be a celebration for ESPN, as it prepares to host its first Super Bowl.
story: This NFL season was supposed to be a celebration for ESPN, as it prepares to host its first Super Bowl. Instead, the spotlight remains on the network’s top football broadcast booth over the tension between longtime partners Joe Buck and analyst Troy Aikman.

While Buck re-signed with ESPN on a long-term, lucrative contract in September, Aikman has been working without an extension to a deal that is set to expire in 2027. The potential breakup of the broadcast team that has worked together for a quarter-century sparked a reported argument in October, and on Thursday Aikman turned up speculation while calling out Buck during his weekly appearance on a Dallas sports radio station.
“I know Joe’s always wanted a one-man booth,” Aikman told 96.7 The Ticket.

Aikman and Buck had spent two decades working together calling games for Fox before they each arrived at ESPN in 2022 as part of an overhaul of the network’s flagship “Monday Night Football” broadcast. Both arrived on five-year contracts. As this season began, Buck told Front Office Sports in September that “Troy Aikman knows that I have his back. … He knows I’m his biggest fan, vice versa.”

Days later, numerous outlets reported Buck had re-signed with the network on a six-year contract worth more than $100 million. Aikman’s deal was set to expire after the Super Bowl. Signs of discord over Buck’s job security at ESPN, and Aikman’s lack of a guaranteed future there, first became public when outlets reported the two had argued before calling an Oct. 12 game between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams.
The Athletic later reported that prior to Buck and Aikman’s argument, Aikman had met with ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro about his future and his relationship with Buck.

“There’s probably a time and a place for all that,” Aikman said of dynamic with Buck on Oct. 15. “I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know if it’s hard to figure out kind of what happened. I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be.”
Pitaro called the timing of media coverage of Buck and Aikman’s falling out “disappointing,” as February’s Super Bowl will be ESPN’s first.

“They’ve done a great job for ESPN, they’ve done a great job for the league, they’ve done a great job for the game, and most importantly, they’ve done a great job for fans. Are we happy about the media coverage recently? Of course not. It’s been disappointing,” Pitaro said this week. “But these guys are professionals, and they’re delivering every week. If you watched it last night, another super high-quality production and telecast, and I’d fully expect that to continue that through the season and through the Super Bowl.”

title: Justice Department seeks dismissal of its lawsuit in Alaska Senate race
summary: The Trump administration had sought to block certification of the election results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan lost. Democrat Mary Peltola won the race.
story: The Trump administration on Thursday asked an appeals court to toss a civil suit it filed last month in Alaska that sought to take the extraordinary step of blocking certification of a state-run election unless the incumbent Senate Republican emerged victorious.
Democratic candidate Mary Peltola ended up winning the race this week.

The lawsuit, filed by the Justice Department in October, followed President Donald Trump’s repeated claims that the inclusion of candidate Dan J. Sullivan on the ballot, alongside Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, was a stunt to “defraud” voters.
In its filing Thursday, the Justice Department asked the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to declare the lawsuit moot, citing Peltola’s victory.

“The United States brought this lawsuit to ensure that the State and its officers fulfill Alaska’s obligation to protect the integrity of its election,” Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward wrote in the filing.
He added that the government “therefore reluctantly acknowledges that there no longer exists any means” of examining whether votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan were intended to be cast for the incumbent.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The ability to prove voters miscast their ballots was seen by many as an insurmountable hurdle when the lawsuit was initially filed.
Before the Trump administration filed its lawsuit, the Alaska Supreme Court ruled in June that Dan J. Sullivan was eligible to remain on the ballot.

On Nov. 1, a federal judge in Alaska rejected the administration’s plea to separate and preserve certain ballots in the Senate election, following a request from the Republican-led state government that the judge permanently dismiss the “meritless lawsuit.”
Trump insisted in the weeks leading up to the election that the two Sullivan candidates would confuse voters and said that he was the one who encouraged the lawsuit.
“I’m the one that said do it,” he told reporters during his midterm blitz in October.

Days after the administration filed its lawsuit, The New York Times reported that Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan to jump into the race. Peltola has denied any wrongdoing.

Trump argued that Peltola should be prosecuted over the allegations, saying on Oct. 28, “This is voter fraud at the highest level,” and that Peltola “should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted, and so should the fake Dan Sullivan.”

Peltola won Alaska’s Senate race with an outright majority, meaning the state did not have to use its ranked choice tabulation process to determine a winner. As a result, the votes cast for either Sullivan did not affect the outcome.
Alaska is not the only place where the Trump administration tried to intervene in the election process, which is conducted by state officials under U.S. law.

In California, the DOJ demanded state officials set aside roughly 20,000 ballots that it alleged were sent to noncitizens. California officials argued that the list of alleged noncitizens provided by the DOJ was outdated and included legitimate voters.
The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s efforts a day before the election, and the Justice Department moved to dismiss its lawsuit later that week.

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Finale Recap: Did the Faithfuls or the Traitors Win?
summary: Read a recap of the two-hour finale of “The Traitors: New Blood” to find out if the Faithfuls were victorious or if the Traitors deceived them and won it all.
story: Warning: Spoilers from the season finale of “The Traitors: New Blood” below…

After weeks of surprising murders and emotional banishments, “The Traitors: New Blood” has come to an end, revealing which player (or players) successfully navigated Alan Cumming’s wicked game and emerged from his castle a winner.

“The Traitors: New Blood,” the first all-civilian season of the reality competition show, wrapped on Thursday, Nov. 19, with an epic two-hour season finale that saw the remaining Faithfuls and Traitors fight for their survival. The season, which was filled with treachery, a tiny Traitor, a mega Traitor, “fruit-gate” and intense Round Table showdowns, saved some of its most thrilling moments for last as the Traitors — Katie and Shane — worked to deceive the Faithfuls one more time.

To make it to the Fire of Truth, the last stage of the game, all the players had to avoid banishment at the remaining two Round Tables, and the Faithfuls had to hope they weren’t the Traitors’ last murder victim.
But after last week’s mission gave the Faithfuls some clues about the Traitors’ identities, Katie and Shane were forced to come up with a risky strategy in the finale to protect themselves.

Did it work? Or did the remaining Faithfuls manage to outlast all the Traitors? Read on for a recap of the supersized finale and find out who joined “The Traitors”’ winner circle nearly $250,000 richer.
The Penultimate Round Table

The first part of the finale, titled “I’m Fighting Till the End,” kicks off with the players returning to the castle after the most recent mission. Clyde begins to test his theory with some of the players that Shane could be a Traitor, sharing that he heard heavy footsteps during the mission. Clyde explains why he suspects Katie is a Traitor, as well. He points out her inability to complete the puzzle in the last mission and notes that the Traitors also struggled to finish their puzzle. Before heading to the Round Table, he asks some of his fellow Faithfuls if they are willing to vote for Katie.

At the Round Table, Alan tells the players that this will be the last time they learn the identity of the player they banish. Shane opens the discussion by criticizing Jay’s strategy throughout the game, revealing that Jay shared his goal was to confuse everyone, including Faithfuls.

When Katie jumps in to make Jay look more suspicious, Clyde suggests that Jay was kept around by the Traitors to be a distraction. He says he believes Katie is a Traitor and mentions the mission puzzle as evidence. Katie admits she isn’t sure how to defend herself before Jay becomes the focus again. Victor points out that Jay voted with the banished Traitors every week and he isn’t open to accepting new information.

All the players vote to banish Jay, who casts a vote for Victor once again, and he is eliminated. On the Circle of Truth, he says, “This has been the ride of my life. I genuinely mean that. When I first came in here, I was a Faithful. But now… I am a Faithful!”
The Traitors’ Final Murder
As the players process the Round Table, Clyde continues to warn them about Katie. He cautions Victor, who confirms he has a crush on Katie, to watch out for her.

In the turret, Shane and Katie discuss their shortlist for murder, which only includes three options since the other players won shields in the previous mission. The two debate whether it is best to remove Victor, Kriste or Clyde from the game.

The final day in the castle arrives. All the players file into the breakfast room except for Clyde, the Traitors’ final casualty of the season. During a flashback, Katie explains that Clyde needed to go because he was coming for both Traitors. She and Shane also hatch a plan to pit Wyatt and Victor against each other before the last Round Table.

When Clyde walks into the confessional and sees a letter from the Traitors waiting for him, he says, “I knew it. Ugh, I’m so sad. But I still think that the Traitors could be Shane and Katie.” Before departing, he adds, “And for all of the Faithful left, don’t let this murder be in vain, ok? Go out there and do what you got to do.”
The Last Mission

For their last mission and final opportunity to add money to the prize pot, the players must locate bunkers around the castle grounds and break into them using dynamite. To do so, they have to split into two teams — one group traveling on wheels and the other via helicopter.

Abbey B. and Katie volunteer to fly high in the helicopter. After directing the group on land to the correct locations, Abbey B. and Katie have to rappel from the side of the helicopter to deliver the dynamite. Despite both having scary moments where they dangled in midair, Abbey B. and Katie complete their task and help raise the prize pot total to $246,300.
The episode ends with Alan advising the players to think about who they can trust.
The Final Round Table

Alan’s ominous words lead into the second part of the finale, fittingly titled “Who Do You Truly Trust?” While preparing for the last Round Table of the season, Victor says he is feeling good. He chats with Shane and Wyatt to confirm that they will all vote to banish Kriste. But during their talk, Victor decides to reveal to Wyatt that he was the player who secretly found a shield in Episode 9. Wyatt is visibly upset that Victor withheld this information from him. Shane says in his confessional that he can use this secret to create tension between Wyatt and Victor.
Wyatt relays his conversation with Victor to Kriste, who then passes it along to Abbey B. Both ladies start to question if Victor is trustworthy.

At the Round Table, Victor says he has been honest the entire game and he is suspicious of Kriste and Katie. Katie is shocked by Victor’s betrayal and says she feels like he has been lying to her. Kriste, meanwhile, rebuffs Victor’s claim that he has been truthful. She calls Victor a liar and a Traitor. “If y’all believe him, you get exactly what you deserve,” she tells her fellow Faithfuls.

But Kriste’s passionate plea has the opposite effect. Some players, including Abbey B., say that Kriste’s intense reaction was out of character and a possible attempt to save herself. Most of the players vote to banish Kriste, who votes for Victor. Katie also joins Kriste in voting to eliminate Victor, which confuses Shane.

Since she cannot reveal her identity, Kriste rises from the table and exits in silence. In her final confessional, she says, “I fought so hard at the end and I was hoping the guys would implode on each other, but they didn’t. It’s just been an amazing ride and it just makes me think what a gift it is to experience all these things in life. And I wouldn’t change a minute of it. I wouldn’t change a second.”
The Fire of Truth

Alan tells the players “one last battle remains”: the Fire of Truth. During their final moments to strategize with each other, Katie says she plans to eliminate Victor so she and Shane can win it all. However, Abbey B. is onto her and tells Wyatt that Katie is a Traitor. Elsewhere, Shane says he wants to finish the game with Katie but he knows the other players do not trust her.

Prior to the Fire of Truth, all the players join Alan for private chats. Shane shares that he wants to win the money so he can take care of his family. Katie explains that she needs the money for security. Victor says he thinks he has what it takes to win, but he needs the other players to trust him. Abbey B. calls the prize money a possible “blessing” that would allow her family to go on a vacation. As for Wyatt, he is more concerned about his allies. He says he doesn’t know if he can count on Victor and that the show has been the most difficult experience of his life.

Alan welcomes the players to the Fire of Truth, where the game will conclude. He explains that the game will end if either they all agree there aren’t any Traitors left or if only two players remain. For the first round, all the players vote to banish again, speculating there is still a Traitor among them. After voting, everyone chooses to eliminate Katie, who votes for Victor.

Katie cries in her confessional as she reflects on her elimination. “I know that wasn’t easy for anyone to do. And it is just a game and I have gained so much from this,” she says. “I am really shocked right now and disappointed in Shane. But I would not change a single thing about this experience other than me losing.”

For the second round, Victor and Shane vote to end the game but Wyatt and Abbey B. want to banish again. They all vote for Victor, who begrudgingly votes for Wyatt. Victor doesn’t have any hard feelings toward his former ally in his exit interview.

“That’s the game right? I got two Traitors out. That’s something I’m proud of,” Victor says in his last confessional. “I got to make some lifelong friends. But sweet, sweet Wyatt, he just couldn’t shake his suspicion of me and I respect it.”

For the third and final round, Wyatt, Abbey B. and Shane vote to end the game. Wyatt becomes emotional and prematurely celebrates their win. Abbey B. is also excited and tells Wyatt and Shane she trusts them. After Wyatt and Abbey B. confirm they are Faithfuls, Shane turns to them and reveals, “I am a Traitor.”

Shane immediately starts apologizing in between sobs. Wyatt and Abbey B. are initially stunned. She then doubles over and weeps. When Wyatt asks for an explanation, Shane says, “I started this game as a Faithful. I was given an ultimatum — either I accept or I get murdered,” adding that he made the choice after Joe was banished. Shane chokes up again before Wyatt and Abbey B. comfort and congratulate him.

In his confessional, Wyatt continues to have a positive attitude. “I really did go into that Round Table believing Shane was a Faithful. A win for the Traitors — that sucks! I am upset about that. But Shane played the perfect game. I can only give him credit,” he says.

Abbey B. is happy for Shane, too. “I am heartbroken and gutted. But you know what? I did the best I could with what I knew,” she shares. “To hear he was a Traitor, I can’t imagine how hard that was for him to look at us and say that. As bad as it hurts, I really am so happy for him. That’s a lot of money! Every single moment of this experience has been magical. So maybe I’m not leaving with the money, but maybe I still win.”

Shane is elated as he celebrates with Alan. “This is life-changing money. I can just finally feel like I’m not drowning under the water. I just feel like I’m barely making it and I can change my life now. Finally, I can actually help people. Thank you so much!” he cheers.
“I did it!” he shouts.
Outside, Shane reunites with the other finalists. Victor says he never expected Shane to be a Traitor. Katie tells Shane she will be ok as long as she gets an invite to his wedding.

After saying everyone is invited to his upcoming nuptials, Shane shares in his last confessional, “I’m so proud of myself. Starting out as a Faithful, then becoming a Traitor, it was so tough. Good things like that don’t really happen to me. This is one of the greatest moments of my life.”

title: Everything We Know About Manni L. Perez, ‘GTA 6’ Female Lead Lucia Caminos
summary: One of the buzziest aspects of the newly released “Grand Theft Auto VI” video game is its introduction of a major playable female character — the first in the “GTA” franchise, which has previously been criticized for its misogynistic content. While developer Rockstar Games has largely kept details about the long-awaited game under wraps, fans this week finally learned the identity of the voice actor behind new character Lucia Caminos.
story: One of the buzziest aspects of the newly released “Grand Theft Auto VI” video game is its introduction of a major playable female character — the first in the “GTA” franchise, which has previously been criticized for its misogynistic content.
While developer Rockstar Games has largely kept details about the long-awaited game under wraps, fans this week finally learned the identity of the voice actor behind new character Lucia Caminos.
Manni Perez, an actor, weightlifter and combat sports athlete, was revealed as the voice actor behind Lucia after she received a Game Awards nomination Nov. 17 for best performance.
Perez has so far not been a large part of the game’s promotion, however she publicly acknowledged her role in “GTA VI” on social media after the news of her nod.
Here’s what we know about Manni Perez.
Perez’s Character Lucia Is a Fugitive
Lucia, one of two characters that players can toggle between, is a a fighter who was recently released from prison and is hoping to thrive on the outside.

“More than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City — but instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands,” the game’s website says.

Together with her boyfriend, Jason, a military veteran who has a history of working with drug runners, Lucia embarks on a Bonnie-and-Clyde-type lifestyle to change her fortunes. However the couple gets caught up in the middle of a criminal conspiracy across the fictional state of Leonida after a robbery goes awry.
Lucia and Jason are then “forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive,” the website says.
Perez Has Made Appearances on Screen, Including in “Law & Order: SVU”
If Lucia’s voice sounds familiar to gamers, it’s likely because they’ve seen Perez before on screen.

The actor, who grew up in New York City and studied at NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts, according to IMBD, has appeared in several high-profile television series, including “Chicago P.D.,” “Blindspot” and Marvel’s “Jessica Jones.”
In a 2020 episode of “SVU,” Perez played Esperanza Morales, a  boxer who was arrested for murder after she attacked her boxing coach, who had been accused of raping a teen.
Perez, who’s a practitioner of MMA, Muay Thai and Brazilian jiu-jitsu, has also worked as a professional belly dancer.
The new game isn’t Perez’s first rodeo with the “Grand Theft Auto” franchise. She previously voiced a blackjack dealer for 2019’s “Grand Theft Auto Online.”
In an interview with the since-shuttered site Paz Magazine, Perez said that that her “biggest fear” was having to portray a “damsel in distress.”

“I’d prefer to play a character that whatever she’s going through, no matter how hard society wants to keep her down, she picks herself up, puts her big girl panties on (preferably cotton [laughs]) and keeps it moving,” she told the outlet.
Perez Has Barely Said Anything About the Game
Perez has said next to nothing about her involvement in the game. It wasn’t until the news of the Game Awards nomination that her identity was revealed.
Still, Perez hasn’t said much about the role aside from sharing a joint post Nov. 19 with the voice actor behind Jason, Dylan Rourke.

“Years witnessing the hardest working and most skilled artisans game making has to offer. We are truly honored to collaborate on this worldwide testament to human creativity, ingenuity, and sheer willpower,” the pair said in a joint Instagram post. “So much learned and so much to learn, keep fighting for what you love, stay humble. See y’all in Leonida.”
